# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **XP & enchanting**: the game gains its first progression currency and a way to spend it, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural XP bar + effect-coloured table sprite, synthesized blip/shimmer). The save schema bumps **v6 → v7** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **XP** (`state.xp`, banked points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level): earned from **mob kills** (hostiles more than passives, the **boss a jackpot**; babies give none, like drops — table in `mobXp.ts`), **mining ores** (scaled by rarity), and **fishing** catches. A green **XP bar** above the hotbar fills toward the next level with the level number over it. Unlike status effects, XP is a long-term currency and is **not cleared on death**
  - **Enchanting**: craft an **Enchanting Table** (2 diamond ore + 4 cobble) and right-click it to open the enchanting panel, then spend XP levels to enchant the **selected** tool/weapon/armor. Deterministic and player-chosen (no random rolls): four enchantments, each up to **level 3** — **Sharpness** (+melee damage), **Protection** (−incoming damage), **Efficiency** (+mining speed), and **Unbreaking** (probabilistically saves durability). Each maps to exactly one existing seam, the same one-reader-per-seam discipline as status effects
  - **Architecture**: enchantments are **per-item-instance data, like durability** (non-stackable gear, slot-cloned on insert), so the inventory algebra and persistence are reused — they ride the existing `SavedSlot` snapshot/restore (validated on load). XP/level math + the award/spend helpers live in `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts`; the readers + `canEnchant`/`applyEnchant` in `lib/game/enchantments.ts`. Enchanting is a new `enchant` command (not a recipe — `craft` produces a fixed result and can't mutate the held instance). The `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is appended (id 52) so existing saved block ids never shift; `xp` and per-slot `enchantments` are additive v7 fields, so pre-XP saves load clean
- **Status effects, brewing & potions**: the game gains its first timed-buff system — six effects, five of them brewed into potions at a new station, all on **zero new assets** (procedural flask/icon sprites + a synthesized "glug"). The save schema bumps **v5 → v6** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **Effects** (`state.effects`, a Map of id → remaining seconds): **Speed** (×1.2 movement), **Strength** (+3 melee damage), **Regeneration** (heals on its own cadence, even at low hunger), **Fire Resistance** (lava can't burn you), **Water Breathing** (lungs stay full, no drowning), and **Poison** (chips you down but **never kills** — floors at half a heart). Each is read at exactly one existing seam (movement speed, attack damage, the lava/oxygen ticks, or a per-tick accumulator), so the simulation stays modular. Re-applying an effect refreshes to the longer remaining time; all are cleared on death
  - **Brewing Stand** (craft 3 cobble + 1 gold ore): a new interactive block — right-click to open its **Brewing** recipes, exactly like a furnace opens smelting, reusing the whole `station`-recipe pipeline. Glass bottles come first (3 glass → 3 bottles), then a bottle + one reagent brews a potion: **feather → Swiftness**, **gunpowder → Strength**, **wheat → Regeneration**, **coal → Fire Resistance**, **raw fish → Water Breathing** (all existing drops/crops, so no new worldgen). Drink with the **F** key (the eat key is potion-aware); drinking consumes the whole bottle
  - **Poison hazard**: eating **rotten flesh** has an 80% chance to poison you — a real downside to the most desperate food. Poison is the only effect with no potion
  - **HUD**: active effects show as a stacked top-left column of procedural icon + m:ss countdown, opposite the minimap, hidden when nothing is active. The projection is cached and rebuilt only when the rounded seconds change, so it re-renders ~1 Hz instead of every frame
  - **Architecture**: effects live in a new `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts` (helpers + `tickStatusEffects`, which runs after `tickHealthRegen` and before the environmental ticks so the fire-resist/water-breathing gates are current). Poison uses a **new** `applyNonLethalDamage` rather than the killing `applyUnmitigatedDamage`. The `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is appended at the end of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift. Effects are additive on save v6 (a pure version bump; pre-effect saves load with none) and **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active
- **Dragon Lord tracker**: while the boss lives, its top-center health HUD now includes a rotating pointer toward it and its horizontal distance in blocks, making it possible to reacquire the fight after terrain or summoned mobs break line of sight. The values are rounded before entering the React snapshot to avoid sub-block render churn. This is transient UI state with **no save-format or worldgen impact**.
- **Fishing**: water was only ever a hazard to avoid — now it's a place to fish, a relaxed renewable food source with the odd lucky find, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural rod/fish sprite + synthesized splashes). **No save-format or worldgen change** — the cast is transient session state and the new items save by string id
  - **Fishing rod** (craft 3 wood + 2 string): right-click while aiming at water to **cast** a bobber. After a random wait it **dips with a splash** (a bite) — right-click again within ~1.2 s to **reel in** a catch; miss the window and it gets away while the bobber keeps fishing
  - **Catch table**: a weighted single pick per bite — mostly **raw fish** (cook it at a furnace, like the meats), sometimes junk (string/bone/seeds/rotten flesh), and rarely a treasure (emerald). Only a successful reel wears the rod
  - **Feedback**: a water-splash particle burst when a fish bites and again on the reel-in, plus the reel sound. Common fish/junk catches stay diegetic (splash + sound + the hotbar count) so frequent fishing never spams the HUD; only the rare **treasure** catch raises a one-line toast
  - **Rod animation**: the rod is no longer static — it winds up and flicks on a cast, holds out over the water while waiting (with a tip twitch on a bite), and yanks back on a reel, in **both first- and third-person**. The bobber **arcs out from the rod tip** to the water and **arcs back** on reel-in (the line is anchored at the rod tip, not the eye), and on a catch the caught item **flies from the bobber to the player**. All render-side — composed onto the pure pose pipeline (`heldItemPose.ts`/`playerPose.ts`) and driven by the fishing events + the `state.fishing` edges, so a silent cancel still reels the bobber back cleanly
  - **Architecture**: the cast is one session-only `state.fishing` field (a bobber position + a bite timer), never serialized and cleared on respawn — the same transient-entity pattern as arrows and thrown spears. A new water-aware `waterSurfaceRaycast` (`lib/world/queries.ts`) finds the surface to aim at, since the normal raycast passes through water. The bobber and a `THREE.Line` fishing line render by reading engine state directly (`lib/game/render/bobberVisuals.ts`); `tryFish`/`tickFishing` (`lib/game/engine/systems/fishing.ts`) drive cast/bite/reel and auto-cancel when the rod is unequipped, the player dies, the water drains, or they stray past the tether
- **Living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread**: the world now renews and heals itself, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural sprout atlas tile + a recolored powder sprite). **No save-format or worldgen change** — every effect is an ordinary block edit riding the save diff, and the hash-pinned worldgen tree code is left untouched
  - **Saplings**: breaking **leaves** now drops a **sapling** (its only yield, ~8% per break) instead of the old placeholder dirt. Right-click a sapling onto grass/dirt to plant it; once it sits on soil it matures into a tree through the existing random-tick system (`SAPLING_GROWTH_CHANCE`). Trees are renewable at last
  - **Bone meal**: grind a skeleton's **bone** into **bone meal** (1 → 3, in the recipe book's Materials section), then right-click it on a sapling to grow the tree **instantly**, or on immature wheat to advance it a random **1–2** stages. A second, renewable use for bones beyond the cursed totem
  - **Grass spread**: exposed **dirt** (a column's top block) **re-grasses** over time when one of its four face-neighbour columns has grass on top, healing mined or built-over terrain
  - **Architecture**: tree building lives in `lib/game/engine/systems/treeGrowth.ts`, shared by the sapling random-tick handler and the bone-meal use; it writes through the `blockChanges` chokepoint (so the tree persists and relights) using the engine rng, and deliberately shares **no** code with worldgen's `placeTrees`, so the generation hashes stay **byte-identical**. Saplings render like wheat — a solid cube with an atlas-painted texture — so there is no new geometry path. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is appended at the end of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift
- **Recipe hints — what's missing and how to get it**: an unaffordable recipe in the inventory's recipe book is no longer a dead end. Hovering one now shows each ingredient as **have / need** (with how many more you're short), and for every missing item a **"how to obtain it"** hint — hunt a mob, craft/smelt/trade, mine, fish, or loot a dungeon — derived once from the existing loot/recipe tables (`lib/game/itemSources.ts`), so new recipes and drops are covered automatically. **This also repairs a latent bug**: recipe rows used the native `disabled` attribute, which suppresses hover events, so even the pre-existing "Requires Furnace/Brewing Stand/Villager" station hint never actually appeared; rows now use `aria-disabled` + a guarded click, staying hoverable while still unclickable. Pure UI plus a derived lookup — **no save-format or worldgen impact**.

### Changed

- **Hostile health visibility and durability**: zombies, skeletons, spiders, and creepers now each have **100 HP**, while the boss has **1000 HP**. Every hostile renders a procedural billboard health bar above its head that tracks damage; the existing boss HUD bar remains. This is transient simulation/render state, so there is **no save-format or worldgen impact**.

### Fixed

- **A corrupt save no longer loads a broken world**: the player position is validated on load (`restorePlayerPosition` in `lib/game/save.ts`) — a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) coordinate is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place. Previously a bad value was copied straight into the player and also slipped past the `position.y < 2` auto-unstuck net (any comparison with NaN is false), so a single corrupt byte could wedge a save.
- **The renderer no longer leaks the block-atlas texture**: `GameRenderer.dispose()` now releases the shared world/glass atlas texture (Three.js `Material.dispose()` does not dispose its map), so switching worlds no longer accumulates orphaned GPU textures.
- **Progress no longer vanishes on a dev hot reload**: the game now persists on component unmount, not only on the 15s autosave timer and `beforeunload`. Turbopack Fast Refresh remounts the game without a page reload (so `beforeunload` never fires), which previously discarded everything collected since the last autosave — most visible as **inventory items disappearing after editing code or rerunning dev**. The unmount save is silent and is deliberately **skipped for Load/Reset**, which intentionally re-read or discard the on-disk save.
- **No setState or reload after unmount**: the React shell tracks and cancels its flash-message and world-reload `setTimeout`s on unmount, so leaving a world mid-timer can't fire a state update or a stray reload on a torn-down component.

## [0.9.0] - 2026-06-14

### Added

- **Villagers & trading**: a passive NPC you can barter with gives gathering an economy, all on **zero new assets** (procedural model + a recolored gem sprite)
  - **Villager** mob: passive like the animals but **doesn't flee** — walk up and **right-click to trade**. It drops nothing if killed (don't murder your shopkeeper) and spawns into the day-one passive population near you
  - **Trading**: the currency is the **emerald**. Right-clicking a villager opens its offers in the inventory's recipe book (re-titled **Trading**). The economy is two-sided — **sell** gathered materials (wheat, coal, leather, gold ore) for emeralds, then **spend** them on goods (bread, torches, arrows, a stone pickaxe, sliver/ruby ore). No use caps; trading is bounded only by what you can gather
  - **Architecture**: a trade is simply a **`station: "villager"` recipe** (`lib/game/trades.ts`, spread into `RECIPES`), so it reuses the entire crafting pipeline and recipe-book UI — opening a villager just sets `craftingStation = "villager"`, and the existing `craft` command runs the trade. The new `"villager"` `MobKind` fills all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables. **No save-format or worldgen change**: villagers are transient, the open trade station is session-only, there are no per-trade use caps to persist, and emerald/traded items save by string id. (Village _structures_ are a possible future addition — villagers currently wander the world among the existing houses rather than spawning in generated settlements, which keeps this change off the worldgen-determinism baseline.)
- **Creepers, TNT & explosions**: the game gains its first explosion system — a sneaking mob that detonates and a craftable demolition charge — all on **zero new assets** (procedural model/atlas + synthesized boom)
  - **Explosion primitive** (`lib/game/engine/systems/explosion.ts`): `explode()` destroys blocks in a power-radius sphere (distance falloff vs each block's blast resistance, sparing bedrock/spawner/lava), then damages the player and mobs out to twice that radius with the same falloff, applies knockback, and emits one `explosion` event. It is **not a new subsystem** — it batches over the existing `blockChanges.set` chokepoint (each cell relights locally, records the save delta) and sets `worldMeshDirty` **once**, so a whole crater costs a single remesh. It only lowers mob hp (never splices), so it is safe to run mid mob-tick; the caller sweeps the dead
  - **Creeper**: a hostile mob that chases silently, then lights a ~1.5 s fuse within ~2.6 blocks (hissing and swelling white), and **explodes** — dying in its own blast and dropping **gunpowder**. Walk past it while primed and the fuse aborts; kill it first to take the gunpowder safely. Burns in daylight like a zombie
  - **TNT**: craft it (4 gunpowder + 1 sand), place it like a block, and **right-click it with a torch** to light a fuse (the torch isn't consumed). It detonates after a delay and **chains** adjacent TNT. Lit fuses are session-only (`state.primedTnt`); a save written mid-fuse reloads with the TNT inert
  - **Minimum hostile spawn distance** (`HOSTILE_SPAWN_MIN_RADIUS`, 16): every hostile spawn (initial + night trickle) now keeps a standoff from the player, so nothing — least of all a creeper — can materialize point-blank
  - The new `"creeper"` `MobKind` fills all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables. Explosions drive a procedural fireball + smoke burst and a synthesized boom; a primed creeper swells and flashes via its `MobState.fuseTimer`. **No save-format or worldgen change**: creepers are spawned, TNT is crafted, fuses are transient, and the new items save by string id
- **Coal & a fuel economy**: a new shallow ore deepens the early game and gives the furnace a real fuel. **Coal ore** is the most common ore (large veins reaching near the surface, mineable with a wood pickaxe) and drops the **coal** fuel item directly. **Charcoal** smelts from a single log as a coal substitute, so a player who hasn't struck coal can still cook. Both fuel the furnace's cooking recipes (chicken/mutton/beef/porkchop) and **torches now cost coal + wood** instead of wood alone. All procedural, **zero new assets** (a dark-flecked atlas tile + a recolored sprite lump)
  - Coal is placed in its own pass (`placeCoal`) on a **dedicated PRNG**, so it never consumes from the shared worldgen `rand` stream — every other ore, tree, and structure stays **byte-identical** to a coal-free world, exactly as deep-cave lava did. Only underground coal cells differ; the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green and only the byte hashes were re-rolled
  - **Worldgen re-baseline**: the new ore changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`** — a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. The save **schema** stays version 5 (coal/charcoal are additive items, coal ore persists in the block diff). `canMineBlock` gates coal behind a wood pickaxe (tier 1, like stone); `GEN.coalConfig` holds its vein tunables
- **Cow & pig farm animals**: two new passive mobs join sheep/chicken/horse, following the same template. **Cows** drop leather + raw beef, **pigs** drop raw porkchop; both raw meats smelt to a cooked form (hunger 8) at a furnace and breed like the others — feed a cow **wheat**, a pig **seeds**. Procedural box models + synthesized moo/grunt calls, **zero new assets**. Mobs and breeding are session-only, the new foods save by string id, so **no save-format or worldgen change**
- **World types**: when creating a world you now pick a generation preset, not just a seed — **Default**, **Superflat** (level builder's canvas), **Amplified** (towering, dramatic relief), or **Islands** (scattered land in a raised sea). Each generates genuinely different terrain over the same biome map; **zero new assets** (the picker reuses the menu chrome)
  - `generateWorld(world, worldType)` forks on the type before any block write via `terrainConfigFor` (`lib/world/generation.ts`), varying only sea level and per-biome surface height; caves, ores, lava, trees, structures, and dungeons are unchanged. The **Default path is byte-identical** to before — existing worlds and the determinism hashes are untouched, so **no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump**. Each new type is pinned by its own SHA-256 baseline plus structural probes (flat is level, amplified spans a wider band, islands floods more of the map while still leaving a dry spawn)
  - The chosen type is stored on `WorldMeta` and in the `SaveData` blob (like `seed`), so a world always regenerates with the type its block-diffs were recorded against. `WorldType` lives in `lib/world/worldTypes.ts`; the schema stays at version 5 (the field is optional, absent ⇒ default)
- **Multiple worlds & player profiles**: the game now opens to a menu instead of dropping straight into one fixed world. A **profile** (name + skin) owns a list of named **worlds**, like user accounts on a shared console — pick a profile, then pick or create a world to play. All client-side in localStorage; **zero new assets** (the menus reuse the existing Minecraft-style chrome and generated skin portraits)
  - **Two-level save hierarchy** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`): a versioned `minecraft_profiles_v1` manifest (`{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }` + `activeProfileId`) and a `minecraft_worlds_v1` index (`{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`), with each world's `SaveData` in its own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. Readers are total — malformed entries are dropped and a dangling active profile is repaired. New-world seeds are resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric → clamped, other text → stable FNV hash). The skin moved off the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key onto the profile; **audio settings stay global**
  - **Menu shell** (`components/GameShell.tsx`, `components/menu/*`): a profile-select → world-select → play state machine with create / rename / delete on both levels (deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset remounts the game subtree via a React `key`, so the engine/renderer are disposed and re-created **without a page reload**. The tab remembers its active world in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes straight back into play while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. The pause menu gains **Save & Quit to Worlds**
  - **Per-world worldgen versioning**: each world records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` it was generated under (`lib/game/config.ts`). A future worldgen change bumps that constant and discards only the affected worlds' stale block-diffs (rebooting them from their seed) — replacing the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` rename, which reset every world. The save _schema_ is unchanged (still version 5)
  - **First run & migration** (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`): a brand-new player is greeted by the create-profile form (name + skin) — their first act is making a profile. An existing single-world save is instead folded into a default "Player" profile (carrying the old skin) plus one "My World"; the legacy blob is copied before the old key is removed, so a failure can't lose data

### Changed

- **Recipe book grouped by category**: the crafting panel's recipe list is no longer one long flat scroll. Recipes are now organized into labeled sections — **Tools, Weapons, Armor, Building, Food, Materials**, then the station-gated **Smelting** and **Trades** — and within each section the recipes you can make right now are listed first, so what's craftable rises to the top. Categories are **derived** from each result item's existing `kind` (station recipes group by station), so adding a recipe needs no extra metadata. Pure presentation: no save-format, worldgen, or recipe-data change (`recipeCategory`/`groupRecipes` in `lib/game/recipes.ts`)

## [0.8.0] - 2026-06-14

### Changed

- Starting play now requires a double-click to acquire pointer lock, preventing an accidental single click from immediately capturing the mouse. No save-format or worldgen impact.
- Emergency unstuck now requires **`Shift` + `U`** instead of a bare `U`, so a stray keypress can no longer teleport the player mid-play. The automatic unstuck safeguard (which fires when wedged in terrain or falling below the world) is unchanged. No save-format or worldgen impact.
- Placed glass now renders as a clear, low-reflection transparent layer. Internal faces between adjacent glass blocks are culled, while neighboring opaque block faces remain visible through it. No save-format or worldgen impact.

### Added

- **Caves & lighting**: caves are no longer lit like the surface — a real per-voxel light system makes underground dark, with torches, deep-cave lava, and drowning as new hazards. All procedural, **zero new assets**
  - **Per-voxel light propagation** (`lib/world/lighting.ts`): each voxel carries packed sky + block light (0–15 each), baked from the blocks at load (top-down sunlight column pass + flood) and patched locally on every edit with a Minecraft-style remove/refill flood. It is a **derived cache, never serialized** (a pure function of `world.blocks`). The mesher emits a per-vertex `aLight` attribute and the world material's shader gates scene-lit terrain by sky exposure (caves go dark) while adding block light back as a glow — so **day/night needs no re-mesh** (the scene sun/hemisphere already scale with daylight)
  - **Torches**: craft four from one wood and place them to light the dark; a torch is a solid block emitting block light 14, so its warm glow floods the surrounding air and survives the night
  - **Lava**: pools in the deepest caves (carved air at or below `lavaLevel`), glowing and emitting max block light. Touching it burns **immediately** for 3 hearts every half-second with no grace period, bypassing armor, and keeps burning briefly after you escape. Worldgen-only — no item, can't be mined
  - **Drowning**: a bubble meter (above the hunger bar) drains over ~15 s while your head is underwater, then deals 1 heart/second until you surface; it refills quickly. Distinct from the existing 60 s body-immersion damage — wading chest-deep never drowns you
  - **Worldgen re-baseline**: the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so the worldgen/meshing hashes were re-rolled and **`SAVE_KEY` bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`** — existing worlds reset. The save _schema_ is unchanged (lighting is derived, lava is worldgen; neither is persisted), so the payload version stays 5. `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` and before `placeDungeons`, keeping the surface byte-identical (structural probes stay green)
- **Spears and non-stackable gear**: seven craftable spear tiers (wood, stone,
  sliver, ruby, sapphire, gold, diamond) have 7-block left-click melee reach and
  can be thrown with right-click/`E`. Throws use procedural projectile meshes,
  gravity, swept mob collision, terrain collision, a cooldown, tiered damage,
  and one durability per throw. Missed throws remain visibly embedded in terrain
  for two seconds, and the faster, flatter trajectory travels farther. All
  durable armor, tools, knives, swords, and spears now occupy one slot across
  drops, crafting, saves, and chests; legacy stacked durable gear is split
  during migration. No save-format or worldgen impact.
- **Wood doors**: craft one from 6 planks and place it on a solid floor to create a thin, two-block-tall panel. Right-click either half to open or close the whole door; open doors rotate onto their hinge edge, while closed doors block players and mobs. Door facing, open state, and both halves persist through the existing block-diff save, and breaking either half removes the whole door and returns one item. Only the player interaction path toggles doors; mobs stop at closed doors and cannot operate them. No save-format or worldgen impact.
- **Water building and exposure damage**: block placement may now replace water cells, so underwater structures can be built against submerged terrain. Remaining continuously immersed for more than 60 seconds starts dealing 3 HP (1.5 hearts) of armor-bypassing damage every second; leaving water fully resets both timers. Exposure is session-only and is not serialized. No save-format or worldgen impact.
- **Endgame & ranged combat**: the game gains its first ranged weapon, ranged enemies, and a true win condition — all on one new transient projectile system, with **no save-format or worldgen change** and **zero new assets** (procedural pixel sprites + synthesized sounds)
  - **Projectile system** (`lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts`, `engine/systems/projectileAI.ts`): arrows are session-only entities (like mobs, never serialized) that integrate under gravity and despawn on a hit, a TTL, or leaving the world. Block collision reuses the world DDA (`voxelRaycast`), which already sweeps the whole segment, so even a very fast arrow can't tunnel a 1-block wall; the entity test is substepped too so a fast arrow can't skip a thin mob between frames. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter — player arrows hit mobs (with knockback), mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated) — so a mob's arrow can never hit the firer or another mob. `tickProjectiles` runs right after `tickMobs` in both the live and dead step branches
  - **Bow & arrows**: craft a **bow** (3 wood + 3 string) and **arrows** (1 stone + 1 wood + 1 feather → 4). Holding a bow makes the attack input fire instead of melee — **instant click-to-fire** (no draw-charge; holding left-click already means mine) at a fixed damage on a short cooldown, spending one arrow and a point of bow durability per shot. The swing animation still plays
  - **Ranged skeletons**: a `ranged` flag on the mob template makes skeletons **kite** — backing off inside a standoff band, holding in the middle, approaching only when far — and loose arrows from across their detect range (leading a moving target) instead of meleeing. Finally distinct from zombies, which stay melee
  - **Endgame boss & victory**: craft a **Cursed Totem** (1 diamond ore + 2 bone + 2 gold ore — the diamond grind's first real goal) and right-click to summon a towering boss nearby (refused if one already walks). It bears down on the player, bites for heavy damage up close, looses a 3-arrow spread at range, periodically conjures minions (capped, under the global hostile cap), and is immune to the daylight burn. Defeating it drops a **Dragon Heart** that crafts the best-in-game **Dragon Sword** (60 attack), fires a one-shot **victory screen**, and shows a top-center **boss health bar** while it lives
  - New `"boss"` `MobKind` touches all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (templates, drops, ambience intervals, ambient + attack sounds). New events (`arrowHit`, `bowFired`, `bossSummoned`, `bossDefeated`, `summonFailed`) drive procedural impact sparks, a conjuring column, a victory burst, and synthesized bow-twang / arrow-tick / boss-roar / victory-fanfare sounds. In-flight arrows render as a pooled extruded-sprite mesh (one shared geometry/material) oriented along their velocity
  - **No version bump**: the boss, its minions, projectiles, and the victory flag are all transient; the new items (bow, arrow, Cursed Totem, Dragon Heart, Dragon Sword) are additive, saved by string id. New tunables live in the `config.ts` "Ranged combat & endgame" group

## [0.7.0] - 2026-06-14

### Added

- **Dungeons & loot**: digging underground now turns up small cobblestone rooms (speckled with mossy cobble) sealed in the rock, well clear of spawn — the game's first real exploration payoff, and a found-loot purpose for chests. All procedural, **zero new assets**
  - Each dungeon holds 1–2 **pre-filled loot chests** and a central **mob spawner**. Loot is tiered (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`): common chests carry food, low ores, and the occasional stone pickaxe (bone always drops, so a chest is never empty); a 25% rare roll adds the payoff — diamond/sapphire ore, a ruby/sapphire sword, helmet/chestplate, or a rare diamond pickaxe
  - **Spawners** drip a hostile (zombie/skeleton/spider) onto the room floor every ~8 s while you're within ~16 blocks, up to 6 clustered nearby (under the global hostile cap). They're time-independent (dungeons are dark); **mining the spawner block out** stops it for good (it's hard and drops nothing). New `mobSpawned` event drives a synthesized low whoosh and a dark conjuring smoke puff
  - New **MossyCobblestone** (mineable into a `mossy_cobble` item, found-only) and **Spawner** blocks, both with procedurally-painted atlas tiles
  - **The lazy-loot design** solves an infinite-loot trap: dungeon chests are placed by deterministic worldgen, so their contents can't live in the block-diff save. Filling them eagerly would let a player empty a chest, reload (the empty chest is dropped from the save), and find fresh loot. Instead the engine fills each chest lazily on **first open or break** — loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` so it's reproducible until you reach it — and records the index in a persisted `lootedChests` set. Gating on "has this been accessed", not "is it currently empty", closes the re-roll. The set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is session-only, re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (which replays the placement math against a dedicated seed-only PRNG and seed-pure terrain estimates, never `highestSolidY`, so it can't diverge from generation)
  - **Save format v5** (additive `lootedChests` field; `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump) and **`SAVE_KEY` bumped `minecraft_save_v5` → `minecraft_save_v6`**: the dungeon worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **existing saved worlds are discarded** (a deliberate, documented re-baseline — worldgen SHA-256 digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled; the structural probes confirm the surface is untouched since dungeons are wholly underground)

# Bun is pinned (not "latest") because the worldgen characterization tests hash
# Math.sin-based noise output, and Math.sin results are engine-defined. Bumping
# the version may legitimately require re-baselining those hashes — see
# docs/testing.md before touching either.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun test
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: bun run test:e2e
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

Yes — I'd cut a release now, and the timing is good. Here's my read.

## Why now

Your `[Unreleased]` section has stacked up a lot since **v0.9.0** (2026-06-14) — four major systems plus fixes, none of it tagged:

- **XP & enchanting** (save schema **v6→v7**)
- **Status effects, brewing & potions** (save schema **v5→v6**)
- **Fishing**, **Living world** (saplings/bone meal/grass spread), **recipe hints**, **hostile health bars**, and 4 bug fixes

That's two save-schema bumps and several headline features sitting un-versioned. Cutting a release now gives you a clean tag to point players at, resets the changelog for the next feature, and is the natural "close the chapter" before we start something new — exactly the right move before adding more.

## What the release involves

It's a small, well-defined chore (no code changes):

1. Bump `package.json` `0.9.0` → new version
2. Rename `## [Unreleased]` → `## [<version>] - 2026-06-21` in `CHANGELOG.md` (it has no bottom link-refs to maintain — simple)
3. Run the full verify gate (lint, typecheck, format:check, test, build) to confirm `main` is actually shippable
4. Commit to `main` (conventional `chore(release):`, no `Co-Authored-By`), then create the `v<version>` git tag

CI (`ci.yml`) only runs on push/PR — there's **no tag-triggered automation**, so pushing the tag and creating a GitHub release are manual and entirely optional.

The fork's `main` has accumulated a large `[Unreleased]` batch since **v0.9.0** (2026-06-14) — four headline systems plus fixes, none of it tagged. This release is a **version chore only — no code changes.** The unreleased work itself is already merged and tested on `main`.

**What's in the release** (already in `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`):
- **XP & enchanting** (save schema **v6→v7**, additive)
- **Status effects, brewing & potions** (save schema **v5→v6**, additive)
- **Fishing**, **Living world** (saplings / bone meal / grass spread), **recipe hints**, **hostile health bars**
- Fixes: corrupt-save position validation, atlas-texture leak, dev-hot-reload persistence, post-unmount setState/reload guard

**Decisions (confirmed with user):** version **0.10.0** (minor bump, matches the one-minor-per-feature-batch cadence); **local commit + tag only** — do not push or create the GitHub release (user pushes/publishes after review).

## Plan

### 1. Bump the version
`package.json` line 3: `"version": "0.9.0"` → `"version": "0.10.0"`.
(No in-app version string exists — grep found only save-schema/profile-manifest versions, which are unrelated and stay as-is.)

### 2. Update `CHANGELOG.md`
- Rename the section heading `## [Unreleased]` (line 5) → `## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21`.
- Add a fresh empty `## [Unreleased]` heading above it for the next cycle (Keep-a-Changelog convention; content stays untouched).
- No bottom link-references exist in this file, so nothing else to update.

### 3. Verify `main` is shippable (the AGENTS.md gate)
Run and confirm green:
```
bun run lint
bun run typecheck
bun run format:check
bun test
bun run build
```
`test:e2e` is optional here — the release touches no renderer/input/React code — but it's cheap insurance; run it if quick.

No `docs/` updates are needed: a release chore changes no behavior, tunable, mechanic, or save format beyond what the already-merged work documented. `CHANGELOG.md` is the only doc that changes.

Single-purpose chore → commits straight to `main` (no branch). Conventional message, body explaining the why, **no `Co-Authored-By` trailer** (AGENTS.md overrides the default trailer rule):

```
chore(release): v0.10.0

Tag the work accumulated since v0.9.0: XP & enchanting, status effects /
brewing / potions, fishing, the living world (saplings, bone meal, grass
spread), recipe hints, and hostile health bars, plus save-load and
dev-reload fixes. The save schema advanced v5 -> v7 across this batch
(both bumps additive). Renames CHANGELOG [Unreleased] to [0.10.0] and
bumps package.json.
```

### 5. Tag locally
Annotated tag: `git tag -a v0.10.0 -m "v0.10.0"`.

### 6. Stop — hand back to the user
Do **not** push and do **not** create the GitHub release. Leave the user the commands:
```
git push origin main --tags
gh release create v0.10.0 --title "v0.10.0" --notes-file <changelog excerpt>
```

**Optional aside (not in this plan unless requested):** the tag list is missing `v0.1.0` and `v0.7.0` (both have changelog entries). Can backfill `v0.7.0` on its release commit if wanted.

## Verification

- `git tag -l | grep v0.10.0` shows the new tag; `git log -1 --stat` shows the release commit touching only `package.json` + `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `head -3 package.json` shows `"version": "0.10.0"`; the `## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21` heading is present with all the unreleased content beneath it.
- The full verify gate ran green before the commit.
- Confirm nothing was pushed (`git status` shows `main` ahead of `origin/main`), and the tag is local only.

## After the release

Return to the original question — choosing the next feature to build (companions & taming, advancements & goals, building & decoration, or water & exploration). That gets its own plan once this release is tagged.

input.prompt:
I'm planning a new "game mode" feature (Survival vs Creative) for monecraft, a Next.js/React/Three.js/TypeScript voxel game. The existing `worldType` (Default/Superflat/Amplified/Islands) is the perfect precedent — it's a per-world setting chosen at creation and persisted. I want to add a `gameMode` field the exact same way.

Please trace and report, with file paths and code excerpts:

1. **WorldType end-to-end plumbing**: Find `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` and trace how `WorldType` flows: where it's defined, how it's chosen at world creation, how it's stored on `WorldMeta` (lib/game/worlds.ts) and in the save blob (`SaveData` in lib/game/types.ts), and how it reaches `generateWorld`/the engine. List every file that references worldType.

2. **World-creation menu UI**: Find the menu components (components/menu/* and components/GameShell.tsx) where a new world is created and the world type is picked. Show the picker UI pattern (how the 4 world types are presented as options) so I can replicate it for a game-mode picker.

3. **Save format & migration**: Look at lib/game/types.ts (SaveDataV1..V7) and lib/game/save.ts. How are optional additive fields added (e.g. worldType)? What's the current schema version, and what would adding an additive `gameMode` field require (migration function pattern)?

4. **WorldMeta & worlds index**: How is per-world metadata (lib/game/worlds.ts, the worlds index in localStorage) structured, and how would a gameMode field be threaded through creation + persistence?

5. **How the engine receives per-world config**: Where does GameEngine get worldType / seed / per-world settings at construction? Where would a gameMode be read by the simulation?

Be specific and quote the relevant code. The goal is a precise map of the "add a per-world enum setting" pattern so I can replicate it for game modes. Medium-thorough.

input.description: Map player systems to gate for Creative
input.prompt:
I'm planning a "Creative mode" for monecraft (a survival voxel game in TypeScript). In Creative mode the player: flies (no gravity, ascend/descend), takes no damage and has no hunger, breaks blocks instantly, and isn't threatened by mobs. I need to find the EXACT seams where a `gameMode === "creative"` check would gate each survival mechanic.

Please explore the engine systems under lib/game/engine/ (especially systems/) and report, with file paths, function names, and code excerpts:

1. **Player movement & physics** (lib/game/engine/systems/playerMotion.ts or similar): How is gravity applied? Where is JUMP_VELOCITY / vertical velocity handled? Where would I add a "fly" mode (gravity off, space=ascend, crouch/shift=descend, double-tap-space to toggle)? Is there any existing noclip/fly/spectator code? How does the emergency-unstuck teleport work (it may hint at how to move the player freely)?

2. **Survival stats & damage** (playerStats.ts): Where are hunger drain, health regen, fall damage, lava damage, drowning/oxygen, and water-immersion damage applied? List each damage source and the single function/seam where it's applied, so I can gate them all behind a "survival only" check (or one central applyDamage chokepoint).

3. **Mining** (mining.ts): How does block-break progress accumulate (hardness, tool tier, MINING_RATE)? Where would "instant break" for creative go? Does mining drop items / consume tool durability — and would creative skip drops?

4. **Mob threat** (systems/mobAI.ts, spawnDirector.ts): Where do hostile mobs decide to aggro/target and where do they deal damage to the player? Where does night-time hostile spawning happen? What's the cleanest seam to make the player non-threatening / non-damageable in creative (mobs ignore player vs mobs deal no damage)?

5. **Death/respawn** (engine step, save.ts): Where is the death check and respawn flow? In creative there's no death — where to short-circuit.

6. **Step order**: Quote the GameEngine.step() order so I understand where these systems run.

Be specific with line references and quote the key code. The goal is an exact list of gate points. Medium-thorough.

input.description: Map inventory and creative item palette

2. **Inventory model** (lib/game/inventory.ts and the engine state): How are inventory slots structured (counts, hotbar vs main inventory, MAX_STACK_SIZE, HOTBAR_SLOTS, INVENTORY_SLOTS)? 5. **Input handling** (where keyboard/mouse input maps to engine commands — likely lib/game/input or the React shell): How are keys bound to actions? Where would I add a fly toggle (double-tap space) and ascend/descend keys? How is the hotbar selection / number keys handled?

**Why it's clean here:**

Good question — and the answer actually clarifies the cleanest design. Let me answer it precisely, because real Minecraft splits this across **two axes**, which resolves the "are Peaceful/Hardcore really modes?" tension neatly.

## How real Minecraft handles it

- **Game mode** (Survival / Creative / Adventure / Spectator): **switchable in-game** — but only if that world has "Allow Cheats" on (via the `/gamemode` command or the F3+F4 switcher). It's set at world creation and can be changed later.
- **Difficulty** (Peaceful / Easy / Normal / Hard): **always switchable in-game** from the Options menu, no cheats needed. So **Peaceful is a *difficulty*, not a game mode.**
- **Hardcore**: a **permanent world flag** chosen at creation, locked to Hard difficulty — death is final (the world is locked/deleted). **Not switchable.**

## The model I'd adopt (faithful + clean)

So your "Creative + Hardcore + Peaceful" maps onto two axes plus a flag — and this is *simpler* than cramming all three into one enum:

| Axis | Values | Switchable? |
|---|---|---|
| **Game mode** | Survival ⇄ Creative | **Yes** — in the pause menu |
| **Difficulty** | Normal ⇄ Peaceful | **Yes** — in the pause menu |
| **Hardcore** | on/off | **No** — fixed at creation (forces Survival; death deletes the world) |

This honors all three of your picks, matches Minecraft's switchability (mode + difficulty live; hardcore permanent), and reuses your existing per-world plumbing. I'll skip a "cheats" gate — it's single-player, so mode is just freely switchable in the pause menu, with the one exception that **Hardcore worlds lock mode and difficulty** (that's the whole point of hardcore).

Let me write this up as the plan.

# Game Modes: Creative, Hardcore & Peaceful

## Context

monecraft is survival-only. We're adding game modes, modeled faithfully on real Minecraft, which splits this across **two switchable axes plus one permanent flag**:

- **Game mode** — `Survival ⇄ Creative` (switchable in the pause menu)
- **Difficulty** — `Normal ⇄ Peaceful` (switchable in the pause menu)
- **Hardcore** — a permanent per-world flag set at creation (forces Survival + Normal; death deletes the world)

This honors the user's choice of "Creative + Hardcore + Peaceful," matches Minecraft's switchability (mode & difficulty live, hardcore permanent), and reuses the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing as its template. **Zero new assets.** Save schema bumps **v7 → v8 (additive)** — no worldgen change.

Single-player, so there's no "cheats" gate: mode/difficulty switch freely in the pause menu. The one exception: a **Hardcore world locks both** (no switching — that's the point).

This is a sizable, cross-cutting feature → it lands on a branch `feat/game-modes` in focused commit slices (data model → Creative → Hardcore → Peaceful → in-game switching → UI/HUD → docs/tests), keeping `bun run lint` green at each slice.

## Data model & plumbing (copy the `worldType` pattern exactly)

`worldType` is the proven template: a per-world enum, validated, stored on `WorldMeta`, persisted in `SaveData` (additive + migration), read by `GameEngine` at boot, picked in `CreateWorldForm`. We mirror it.

1. **New `lib/game/gameModes.ts`** — `GameMode = "survival" | "creative"`, `Difficulty = "normal" | "peaceful"`, plus `isGameMode`/`isDifficulty` validators and `GAME_MODE_PRESETS` / `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` (`{ id, label, blurb }`) for the pickers (parallels `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`).
2. **`WorldMeta`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore: boolean` — the *creation-time* values (for first boot before a save exists + world-card badges). Extend `sanitizeWorld` (coerce unknown → `survival`/`normal`/`false`) and `createWorld` deps, exactly like `worldType`.
3. **`SaveData` v8** (`lib/game/types.ts`): `SaveDataV8 = Omit<SaveDataV7,"version"> & { version: 8; gameMode?: GameMode; difficulty?: Difficulty; hardcore?: boolean }`. The *current* (possibly-switched) values are authoritative here.
4. **Migration** (`lib/game/save.ts`): `migrateSaveV7toV8` = pure bump; extend the `readSave` chain and point `SaveData` at v8.
5. **`GameEngine`** (`GameEngine.ts`): add `gameMode`/`difficulty`/`hardcore` to `GameEngineOptions`; constructor resolves `save ?? options ?? default` (save wins on restore, like `worldType`); `serialize()` writes all three.
6. **`GameState`** (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore`, and transient `isFlying: boolean`. Expose `gameMode`/`difficulty`/`hardcore`/`isFlying` on the React snapshot so the HUD/menus can read them.

## Creative mode — gate the survival seams behind `gameMode === "creative"`

The damage/consume seams are already centralized; Creative switches them off as a group. Gate points (all confirmed in exploration):

- **No damage / no hunger** — `lib/game/engine/systems/playerStats.ts`: skip `tickHungerDrain`, force full health in `tickHealthRegen`, and gate the `applyDamage(...)` calls in `tickWaterExposure`/`tickLavaExposure`/`tickOxygen`. `playerMotion.ts`: gate fall-damage (~L127) and void-damage (~L134).
- **No death** — `lib/game/engine/systems/playerLife.ts`: early-`return false` in `applyDamageWithArmor` + `applyUnmitigatedDamage` when creative.
- **Instant build, no drops, no durability** — `mining.ts`: in `tickMining`, skip the hardness accumulation (break immediately) and gate `addBlockDrop`/`consumeToolDurability`.
- **No item consumption on placement** — `mining.ts` `placeSelectedBlock`: gate the single `adjustSlotCount(..., -1, ...)` decrement.
- **Flight** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isFlying`, replace the gravity block with vertical control (Space = ascend, crouch = descend, else hover at `velocity.y = 0`) at `FLY_SPEED`. `inputController.ts`: double-tap **Space** (≤300 ms) dispatches `toggleFlight` (creative only; ignored otherwise). Entering survival forces `isFlying = false`.
- **No hostiles** — shared with Peaceful below.

**Creative inventory palette** — a new tab in `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` listing all of `ITEM_DEFS` (from `lib/game/items.ts`) grouped by `kind`, reusing the existing `inv-grid` slot buttons; click an item → `adjustSlotCount(+stack, preferredSlot)` (use `createSlot`). Add a small search/filter box. Shown when `gameMode === "creative"` in place of the recipe book.

## Hardcore — permanent permadeath flag

- Fixed at creation; forces `gameMode = "survival"`, `difficulty = "normal"`, and is **not switchable**.
- On death in a hardcore world: **do not respawn** — instead the engine leaves `isDead` set and surfaces it; the React shell (`useMinecraftGame.ts` / `GameShell.tsx`) detects `isDead && hardcore`, shows a "Game Over" screen, calls the existing `deleteWorld(...)` (`lib/game/worlds.ts`), and returns to the world-select menu. Gate `tickRespawnTimer` so it never auto-revives a hardcore player.
- World-card badge: "Hardcore" (e.g. tinted). Optionally tint the HUD hearts.

## Peaceful — a difficulty (no hostiles), shares Creative's spawn gate

- Gate hostile spawning in `spawnDirector.ts` (`tickHostileSpawnDirector` + the dungeon `tickSpawnerDirector`): early-return when `difficulty === "peaceful"` **or** `gameMode === "creative"`.
- Clear/despawn existing hostiles on entering Peaceful (so night turns safe immediately).
- monecraft hunger doesn't deal starvation damage today (it only gates regen), so no extra hunger handling is needed for Peaceful.

## In-game switching (pause menu) + state-reset on switch

- Pause menu (the existing pause component with Save & Quit / volume) gains a **Game Mode** selector (Survival/Creative) and **Difficulty** selector (Normal/Peaceful). Both are **hidden/locked for hardcore worlds**.
- New engine commands `setGameMode` / `setDifficulty`. On switch, reset transient state so no queued damage or stuck flight leaks across:
  - → Creative: `isFlying = false`, hearts/hunger forced full, and reset the lava/void/water/drown timers in `state.timers`.
  - → Survival: `isFlying = false` (gravity resumes, player falls), hearts/hunger restored to full, same timer reset.
  - → Peaceful/Normal: clear hostiles on entering Peaceful; nothing special re-entering Normal.

## UI surfaces

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: add a game-mode grid + difficulty grid + a hardcore toggle, mirroring the existing `world-type-grid` markup. Thread choices through `WorldSelect.onCreate` → `createWorld({ gameMode, difficulty, hardcore })`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: world cards show mode/difficulty/hardcore badges (like the current `worldType` sub-label).
- HUD (`components/game/*`): hide hearts + hunger bars in Creative; show a subtle "Creative" / flying indicator; hardcore heart tint.
- Pause menu component: the two selectors above.

## Config tunables (`lib/game/config.ts`)

- `FLY_SPEED` (≈12–16 blocks/s) and `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (0.3). Group under a new "Game modes / creative flight" comment block.

## Representative files to modify

New: `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, `components/game/CreativeInventoryTab.tsx` (or inline in `InventoryPanel.tsx`).
Edited: `lib/game/types.ts`, `lib/game/save.ts`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`, `lib/game/engine/state.ts`, `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`, `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `lib/game/config.ts`, `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`, systems `playerMotion.ts` / `playerStats.ts` / `playerLife.ts` / `mining.ts` / `spawnDirector.ts` / `mobAI.ts` / `projectileAI.ts`, and components `CreateWorldForm.tsx` / `WorldSelect.tsx` / `InventoryPanel.tsx` / the pause menu / HUD.

## Tests (`*.test.ts`, colocated)

- Save migration `v7 → v8` (pure bump; old save loads as survival/normal/non-hardcore).
- Creative gates: no damage from lava/void/fall/water/drown, no death, instant break, no drop, no durability loss, no item consumed on placement.
- Flight: `toggleFlight` only flips in creative; ascend/descend changes `velocity.y`; entering survival clears `isFlying`.
- Hardcore: death sets `isDead` and does **not** respawn; the shell signal is exposed.
- Peaceful: `tickHostileSpawnDirector` no-ops at night; existing hostiles cleared on switch.
- Mode/difficulty switch resets timers + hearts/hunger.
- Update `config.test.ts` integrity (new enums/presets exhaustive; `ITEM_DEFS` palette coverage).

## Docs (ship with the change — part of the gate)

- `docs/manual.md`: new "Game Modes" section (Creative/flight/palette, Hardcore, Peaceful, switching).
- `docs/reference.md`: a modes/difficulty table.
- `docs/save-format.md`: v8 fields + migration.
- `docs/tuning.md`: `FLY_SPEED` / double-tap window.
- `README.md`: fly controls (double-tap Space, Space/crouch).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: add to `[Unreleased]`.

## Verification

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green; `bun run test:e2e` (touches input + React shell).
- Manual pass (per docs/testing.md, since input/visuals change): create a **Creative** world → double-tap Space to fly, build from the palette with no item loss, stand in lava/jump off a cliff and take no damage, confirm hearts/hunger hidden. Create a **Hardcore** world → die and confirm the world is deleted and you return to the menu. Create a **Peaceful** world → confirm no hostiles spawn at night. In a normal world, switch Survival⇄Creative and Normal⇄Peaceful from the pause menu and confirm state resets cleanly.

## After this lands

The other next-feature candidates remain on the table (companions & taming, advancements & goals, building & decoration, water & exploration) for a future release.

Agreed — if we're modeling on Minecraft, follow its actual four game modes rather than inventing our own set. I've redesigned around that. Here's my thinking, then the rewritten plan.

## The four modes, mapped to monecraft

The clean structure is: **one `gameMode` axis with four values**, plus the two orthogonal things Minecraft keeps *separate* from game mode — **Difficulty** (where Peaceful lives) and the **Hardcore** flag. So your earlier Creative/Hardcore/Peaceful picks all still land; they just sit on their correct axes.

| Behavior | Survival | Creative | Adventure | Spectator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Damage / hunger / death | yes | **no** | yes | **no** |
| Break blocks | yes | instant, no drop | **no** | no |
| Place blocks | yes (consumes) | **no consume** | **no** | no |
| Flight | no | yes | no | **noclip** (pass through blocks) |
| Terrain collision | yes | yes | yes | **no** |
| Interact (doors/chests/trade/attack/eat/fish) | yes | yes | yes | **no** |
| Mobs threaten you | yes | no | yes | no |
| Inventory | normal | all-items palette | normal | hidden |

Plus **Hardcore** (survival + permadeath, fixed at creation) and **Peaceful** (difficulty: no hostile spawns, switchable).

## My honest take on the four

- **Creative** — the big win; do this well.
- **Spectator** — genuinely fun here (free-cam noclip flythrough of your world). Most new code: noclip = *disable terrain collision*, plus block all interaction and render the player translucent.
- **Adventure** — faithful to include, but **low value in single-player**: its whole purpose is locking block editing on *shared custom maps*, which this game doesn't have. The upside: it's nearly free — just gate break + place on top of survival. I'd keep it for completeness but it's the one I'd cut first if you want leaner scope.

I'm keeping the implementation clean with mode **predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`) in one file, so each system gates on intent rather than scattering `mode === "x"` checks. This is now a sizable feature, so the plan sequences it into reviewable slices.

# Game Modes — Minecraft's four modes (+ Difficulty & Hardcore)

## Context

monecraft is survival-only. We're adding game modes modeled on real Minecraft, which structures this as **three independent things**:

- **Game mode** (one axis, four values): `Survival` · `Creative` · `Adventure` · `Spectator` — switchable in the pause menu.
- **Difficulty**: `Normal ⇄ Peaceful` — switchable in the pause menu (Peaceful = no hostile spawns).
- **Hardcore**: a permanent per-world flag set at creation (forces Survival + Normal; death deletes the world).

This follows Minecraft's real structure and still delivers the user's earlier Creative / Hardcore / Peaceful picks — now on their correct axes. **Zero new assets.** Save schema bumps **v7 → v8 (additive)**; no worldgen change. Single-player, so no "cheats" gate — mode/difficulty switch freely, except a **Hardcore world locks both**.

**Scope note:** this is large and cross-cutting → branch `feat/game-modes`, landed in focused, individually-green commit slices (data model → predicates → Creative → Spectator → Adventure → Hardcore → Peaceful → in-game switching → UI/HUD → docs/tests). Adventure is the cheapest and lowest-value (its purpose — locking block edits on shared custom maps — doesn't apply to a single-player game); it can be dropped to trim scope without affecting the rest.

## Mode behavior matrix

| Behavior | Survival | Creative | Adventure | Spectator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Damage / hunger / death | ✓ | �— | ✓ | �— |
| Break blocks | ✓ | instant, no drop/durability | ✕ | ✕ |
| Place blocks | ✓ (consumes) | ✓ (no consume) | ✕ | ✕ |
| Flight | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ noclip |
| Terrain collision | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Interact (door/chest/trade/attack/eat/fish) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Mobs threaten player | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Inventory | normal | all-items palette | normal | hidden |
| Player render | solid | solid | solid | translucent |

## Mode predicates (the core abstraction)

New `lib/game/gameModes.ts` — `GameMode = "survival" | "creative" | "adventure" | "spectator"`, `Difficulty = "normal" | "peaceful"`, validators, and `GAME_MODE_PRESETS` / `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` (`{ id, label, blurb }`, parallel to `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS`). Plus intent predicates each system gates on (so no scattered string compares):

- `takesDamage(mode)` = survival | adventure
- `canEditBlocks(mode)` = survival | creative (adventure & spectator: false)
- `freeBuild(mode)` = creative (instant break, no drop, no consume)
- `canInteract(mode)` = mode !== spectator
- `canFly(mode)` = creative | spectator
- `isNoclip(mode)` = spectator
- `usesInventory(mode)` = mode !== spectator
- `mobsThreaten(mode)` = survival | adventure

## Data model & plumbing (copy the `worldType` pattern)

`worldType` is the proven per-world-enum template (validator → `WorldMeta` → `SaveData` additive + migration → `GameEngine` boot → `CreateWorldForm`). Mirror it:

1. **`WorldMeta`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore` (creation-time values for first boot + world-card badges); extend `sanitizeWorld` (coerce unknown → `survival`/`normal`/`false`) and `createWorld` deps.
2. **`SaveData` v8** (`lib/game/types.ts`): `version: 8; gameMode?; difficulty?; hardcore?` — authoritative *current* values (mode/difficulty may have been switched).
3. **Migration** (`lib/game/save.ts`): `migrateSaveV7toV8` pure bump; extend the `readSave` chain; repoint `SaveData` to v8.
4. **`GameEngine`** (`GameEngine.ts`): add the three to `GameEngineOptions`; resolve `save ?? options ?? default` (save wins on restore); `serialize()` writes them.
5. **`GameState`** (`engine/state.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore`, transient `isFlying`; expose all on the React snapshot for HUD/menus.

## Creative — gate via predicates

- **No damage / hunger / death** — `playerStats.ts` (`tickHungerDrain` skip; `tickHealthRegen` force full; gate `applyDamage` in water/lava/oxygen ticks), `playerMotion.ts` (fall + void damage), `playerLife.ts` (`applyDamageWithArmor`/`applyUnmitigatedDamage` early-return) — all gated on `!takesDamage(mode)`.
- **Free build** — `mining.ts` `tickMining`: when `freeBuild`, break instantly, skip `addBlockDrop` + `consumeToolDurability`; `placeSelectedBlock`: skip the `adjustSlotCount(-1)` decrement.
- **Flight** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isFlying`, replace gravity with vertical control (Space ascend / crouch descend / hover) at `FLY_SPEED`. `inputController.ts`: double-tap Space → `toggleFlight` when `canFly`.
- **All-items palette** — new tab in `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` listing `ITEM_DEFS` grouped by `kind` (reuse `inv-grid` buttons + `createSlot`/`adjustSlotCount`), with a search box; shown when `gameMode === "creative"`.

## Spectator — noclip free-cam

- **Always flying, noclip** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isNoclip`, skip the terrain collision-resolution/depenetration step and integrate position straight from velocity; force `isFlying` true, never grounded; reuse the Creative fly controls.
- **Invulnerable / no hunger / no death** — same `!takesDamage` gates as Creative.
- **No interaction at all** — gate all world-affecting commands in `GameEngine.dispatch` and `tickMining` behind `canInteract`: mining, placing, attack, use/eat/fish/trade/interact all no-op; only movement, camera, pause, and the mode menu remain.
- **Mobs ignore the player** — `mobAI.ts`/`projectileAI.ts`/`spawnDirector.ts` gate aggro + player-damage on `mobsThreaten(mode)` (false for Creative & Spectator).
- **Translucent player** — renderer: when spectator, draw the player model semi-transparent (or hidden in third-person); first-person is unchanged. Hide the hotbar/HUD bars.

## Adventure — survival minus terrain editing

- Identical to Survival (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trade/eat/fish all work) **except block break + place are disabled**: the `canEditBlocks` gate already added to `tickMining` (break) and `placeSelectedBlock` covers it. No flight, normal HUD. Essentially free once the predicate gates exist.

## Hardcore — permanent permadeath flag

- Fixed at creation; forces `gameMode = "survival"`, `difficulty = "normal"`, not switchable.
- On death in a hardcore world: don't respawn — leave `isDead` set and surface it; the React shell (`useMinecraftGame.ts` / `GameShell.tsx`) detects `isDead && hardcore`, shows a "Game Over" screen, calls the existing `deleteWorld(...)` (`lib/game/worlds.ts`), and returns to the world-select menu. Gate `tickRespawnTimer` so a hardcore player never auto-revives. World-card "Hardcore" badge; optional heart tint.

## Peaceful — a difficulty (no hostiles)

- Gate hostile spawning in `spawnDirector.ts` (`tickHostileSpawnDirector` + dungeon `tickSpawnerDirector`): early-return when `difficulty === "peaceful"` **or** `!mobsThreaten(mode)`. Clear existing hostiles on entering Peaceful. (monecraft hunger doesn't deal starvation damage, so no extra hunger handling needed.)

## In-game switching + state reset

- Pause menu gains a **Game Mode** selector (4 options) and **Difficulty** selector (2) — both hidden/locked for hardcore worlds.
- New `setGameMode` / `setDifficulty` engine commands. On switch, reset transient state so nothing leaks:
  - Entering a no-damage mode (Creative/Spectator): hearts/hunger forced full; reset lava/void/water/drown timers in `state.timers`.
  - Entering Spectator: `isFlying = true`, noclip on. Leaving Spectator: snap out of noclip (resolve out of any solid block, reuse the existing auto-unstuck depenetration), `isFlying = false`.
  - Entering Survival/Adventure: `isFlying = false` (gravity resumes); restore full hearts/hunger.
  - Entering Peaceful: clear hostiles.

## UI surfaces

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: a 4-option game-mode grid + 2-option difficulty grid + a Hardcore toggle (mirroring the `world-type-grid` markup). Thread through `WorldSelect.onCreate` → `createWorld({ gameMode, difficulty, hardcore })`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: world-card badges for mode/difficulty/hardcore.
- HUD (`components/game/*`): hide hearts + hunger in Creative/Spectator; hide the hotbar in Spectator; small "Creative"/"Spectator"/flying indicator; "Game Over" screen for hardcore death.
- Pause menu: the two selectors (locked for hardcore).

## Config tunables (`lib/game/config.ts`)

`FLY_SPEED` (≈12–16) and `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (0.3), under a new "Game modes / flight" group.

## Representative files

New: `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, `components/game/CreativeInventoryTab.tsx` (or inline).
Edited: `lib/game/types.ts`, `save.ts`, `worlds.ts`, `engine/state.ts`, `engine/GameEngine.ts`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`, `config.ts`, `input/inputController.ts`; systems `playerMotion.ts` / `playerStats.ts` / `playerLife.ts` / `mining.ts` / `spawnDirector.ts` / `mobAI.ts` / `projectileAI.ts`; the player renderer; components `CreateWorldForm.tsx` / `WorldSelect.tsx` / `InventoryPanel.tsx` / pause menu / HUD.

## Tests (colocated `*.test.ts`)

- Migration `v7 → v8` (old save → survival/normal/non-hardcore).
- Predicates table (each mode's flags).
- Creative: no damage, instant break, no drop/durability, no consume on place; palette inserts.
- Spectator: noclip (moves through a solid block), invulnerable, all interaction commands no-op, mobs don't aggro.
- Adventure: damage still applies; break + place are blocked; combat/interaction still work.
- Flight: `toggleFlight` only when `canFly`; ascend/descend change `velocity.y`.
- Hardcore: death sets `isDead`, no respawn, shell signal surfaced.
- Peaceful: hostile spawn directors no-op; hostiles cleared on switch.
- Switch resets timers + hearts/hunger + noclip exit. Update `config.test.ts` integrity (exhaustive presets, `ITEM_DEFS` palette coverage).

## Docs (ship with the change — part of the gate)

`docs/manual.md` (new "Game Modes" section: the four modes, flight, palette, Hardcore, Peaceful, switching), `docs/reference.md` (modes/difficulty table), `docs/save-format.md` (v8 fields + migration), `docs/tuning.md` (`FLY_SPEED` + double-tap), `README.md` (fly controls), `CHANGELOG.md` (`[Unreleased]`).

## Verification

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green; `bun run test:e2e` (touches input + shell).
- Manual pass (input/visual change): **Creative** — fly (double-tap Space), build from palette with no item loss, take no damage, hearts/hunger hidden. **Spectator** — fly through terrain, can't break/interact, mobs ignore you, player translucent. **Adventure** — take damage and fight mobs, but can't break/place blocks. **Hardcore** — die → world deleted → back to menu. **Peaceful** — no hostiles at night. **Switching** — flip modes/difficulty in the pause menu and confirm clean state resets; confirm hardcore worlds lock the selectors.

## After this lands

Other candidates remain for later: companions & taming, advancements & goals, building & decoration, water & exploration.

# Game Modes: Creative, Hardcore & Peaceful

## Context

monecraft is survival-only. We're adding game modes, modeled faithfully on real Minecraft, which splits this across **two switchable axes plus one permanent flag**:

- **Game mode** — `Survival ⇄ Creative` (switchable in the pause menu)
- **Difficulty** — `Normal ⇄ Peaceful` (switchable in the pause menu)
- **Hardcore** — a permanent per-world flag set at creation (forces Survival + Normal; death deletes the world)

This honors the user's choice of "Creative + Hardcore + Peaceful," matches Minecraft's switchability (mode & difficulty live, hardcore permanent), and reuses the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing as its template. **Zero new assets.** Save schema bumps **v7 → v8 (additive)** — no worldgen change.

Single-player, so there's no "cheats" gate: mode/difficulty switch freely in the pause menu. The one exception: a **Hardcore world locks both** (no switching — that's the point).

This is a sizable, cross-cutting feature → it lands on a branch `feat/game-modes` in focused commit slices (data model → Creative → Hardcore → Peaceful → in-game switching → UI/HUD → docs/tests), keeping `bun run lint` green at each slice.

## Data model & plumbing (copy the `worldType` pattern exactly)

`worldType` is the proven template: a per-world enum, validated, stored on `WorldMeta`, persisted in `SaveData` (additive + migration), read by `GameEngine` at boot, picked in `CreateWorldForm`. We mirror it.

1. **New `lib/game/gameModes.ts`** — `GameMode = "survival" | "creative"`, `Difficulty = "normal" | "peaceful"`, plus `isGameMode`/`isDifficulty` validators and `GAME_MODE_PRESETS` / `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` (`{ id, label, blurb }`) for the pickers (parallels `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`).
2. **`WorldMeta`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore: boolean` — the *creation-time* values (for first boot before a save exists + world-card badges). Extend `sanitizeWorld` (coerce unknown → `survival`/`normal`/`false`) and `createWorld` deps, exactly like `worldType`.
3. **`SaveData` v8** (`lib/game/types.ts`): `SaveDataV8 = Omit<SaveDataV7,"version"> & { version: 8; gameMode?: GameMode; difficulty?: Difficulty; hardcore?: boolean }`. The *current* (possibly-switched) values are authoritative here.
4. **Migration** (`lib/game/save.ts`): `migrateSaveV7toV8` = pure bump; extend the `readSave` chain and point `SaveData` at v8.
5. **`GameEngine`** (`GameEngine.ts`): add `gameMode`/`difficulty`/`hardcore` to `GameEngineOptions`; constructor resolves `save ?? options ?? default` (save wins on restore, like `worldType`); `serialize()` writes all three.
6. **`GameState`** (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore`, and transient `isFlying: boolean`. Expose `gameMode`/`difficulty`/`hardcore`/`isFlying` on the React snapshot so the HUD/menus can read them.

## Creative mode — gate the survival seams behind `gameMode === "creative"`

The damage/consume seams are already centralized; Creative switches them off as a group. Gate points (all confirmed in exploration):

- **No damage / no hunger** — `lib/game/engine/systems/playerStats.ts`: skip `tickHungerDrain`, force full health in `tickHealthRegen`, and gate the `applyDamage(...)` calls in `tickWaterExposure`/`tickLavaExposure`/`tickOxygen`. `playerMotion.ts`: gate fall-damage (~L127) and void-damage (~L134).
- **No death** — `lib/game/engine/systems/playerLife.ts`: early-`return false` in `applyDamageWithArmor` + `applyUnmitigatedDamage` when creative.
- **Instant build, no drops, no durability** — `mining.ts`: in `tickMining`, skip the hardness accumulation (break immediately) and gate `addBlockDrop`/`consumeToolDurability`.
- **No item consumption on placement** — `mining.ts` `placeSelectedBlock`: gate the single `adjustSlotCount(..., -1, ...)` decrement.
- **Flight** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isFlying`, replace the gravity block with vertical control (Space = ascend, crouch = descend, else hover at `velocity.y = 0`) at `FLY_SPEED`. `inputController.ts`: double-tap **Space** (≤300 ms) dispatches `toggleFlight` (creative only; ignored otherwise). Entering survival forces `isFlying = false`.
- **No hostiles** — shared with Peaceful below.

**Creative inventory palette** — a new tab in `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` listing all of `ITEM_DEFS` (from `lib/game/items.ts`) grouped by `kind`, reusing the existing `inv-grid` slot buttons; click an item → `adjustSlotCount(+stack, preferredSlot)` (use `createSlot`). Add a small search/filter box. Shown when `gameMode === "creative"` in place of the recipe book.

## Hardcore — permanent permadeath flag

- Fixed at creation; forces `gameMode = "survival"`, `difficulty = "normal"`, and is **not switchable**.
- On death in a hardcore world: **do not respawn** — instead the engine leaves `isDead` set and surfaces it; the React shell (`useMinecraftGame.ts` / `GameShell.tsx`) detects `isDead && hardcore`, shows a "Game Over" screen, calls the existing `deleteWorld(...)` (`lib/game/worlds.ts`), and returns to the world-select menu. Gate `tickRespawnTimer` so it never auto-revives a hardcore player.
- World-card badge: "Hardcore" (e.g. tinted). Optionally tint the HUD hearts.

## Peaceful — a difficulty (no hostiles), shares Creative's spawn gate

- Gate hostile spawning in `spawnDirector.ts` (`tickHostileSpawnDirector` + the dungeon `tickSpawnerDirector`): early-return when `difficulty === "peaceful"` **or** `gameMode === "creative"`.
- Clear/despawn existing hostiles on entering Peaceful (so night turns safe immediately).
- monecraft hunger doesn't deal starvation damage today (it only gates regen), so no extra hunger handling is needed for Peaceful.

## In-game switching (pause menu) + state-reset on switch

- Pause menu (the existing pause component with Save & Quit / volume) gains a **Game Mode** selector (Survival/Creative) and **Difficulty** selector (Normal/Peaceful). Both are **hidden/locked for hardcore worlds**.
- New engine commands `setGameMode` / `setDifficulty`. On switch, reset transient state so no queued damage or stuck flight leaks across:
  - → Creative: `isFlying = false`, hearts/hunger forced full, and reset the lava/void/water/drown timers in `state.timers`.
  - → Survival: `isFlying = false` (gravity resumes, player falls), hearts/hunger restored to full, same timer reset.
  - → Peaceful/Normal: clear hostiles on entering Peaceful; nothing special re-entering Normal.

## UI surfaces

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: add a game-mode grid + difficulty grid + a hardcore toggle, mirroring the existing `world-type-grid` markup. Thread choices through `WorldSelect.onCreate` → `createWorld({ gameMode, difficulty, hardcore })`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: world cards show mode/difficulty/hardcore badges (like the current `worldType` sub-label).
- HUD (`components/game/*`): hide hearts + hunger bars in Creative; show a subtle "Creative" / flying indicator; hardcore heart tint.
- Pause menu component: the two selectors above.

## Config tunables (`lib/game/config.ts`)

- `FLY_SPEED` (≈12–16 blocks/s) and `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (0.3). Group under a new "Game modes / creative flight" comment block.

## Representative files to modify

New: `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, `components/game/CreativeInventoryTab.tsx` (or inline in `InventoryPanel.tsx`).
Edited: `lib/game/types.ts`, `lib/game/save.ts`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`, `lib/game/engine/state.ts`, `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`, `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `lib/game/config.ts`, `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`, systems `playerMotion.ts` / `playerStats.ts` / `playerLife.ts` / `mining.ts` / `spawnDirector.ts` / `mobAI.ts` / `projectileAI.ts`, and components `CreateWorldForm.tsx` / `WorldSelect.tsx` / `InventoryPanel.tsx` / the pause menu / HUD.

## Tests (`*.test.ts`, colocated)

- Save migration `v7 → v8` (pure bump; old save loads as survival/normal/non-hardcore).
- Creative gates: no damage from lava/void/fall/water/drown, no death, instant break, no drop, no durability loss, no item consumed on placement.
- Flight: `toggleFlight` only flips in creative; ascend/descend changes `velocity.y`; entering survival clears `isFlying`.
- Hardcore: death sets `isDead` and does **not** respawn; the shell signal is exposed.
- Peaceful: `tickHostileSpawnDirector` no-ops at night; existing hostiles cleared on switch.
- Mode/difficulty switch resets timers + hearts/hunger.
- Update `config.test.ts` integrity (new enums/presets exhaustive; `ITEM_DEFS` palette coverage).

## Docs (ship with the change — part of the gate)

- `docs/manual.md`: new "Game Modes" section (Creative/flight/palette, Hardcore, Peaceful, switching).
- `docs/reference.md`: a modes/difficulty table.
- `docs/save-format.md`: v8 fields + migration.
- `docs/tuning.md`: `FLY_SPEED` / double-tap window.
- `README.md`: fly controls (double-tap Space, Space/crouch).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: add to `[Unreleased]`.

## Verification

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green; `bun run test:e2e` (touches input + React shell).
- Manual pass (per docs/testing.md, since input/visuals change): create a **Creative** world → double-tap Space to fly, build from the palette with no item loss, stand in lava/jump off a cliff and take no damage, confirm hearts/hunger hidden. Create a **Hardcore** world → die and confirm the world is deleted and you return to the menu. Create a **Peaceful** world → confirm no hostiles spawn at night. In a normal world, switch Survival⇄Creative and Normal⇄Peaceful from the pause menu and confirm state resets cleanly.

## After this lands

The other next-feature candidates remain on the table (companions & taming, advancements & goals, building & decoration, water & exploration) for a future release.
