# Game Modes — Minecraft's four modes (+ Difficulty & Hardcore)

## Context

monecraft is survival-only. We're adding game modes modeled on real Minecraft, which structures this as **three independent things**:

- **Game mode** (one axis, four values): `Survival` · `Creative` · `Adventure` · `Spectator` — switchable in the pause menu.
- **Difficulty**: `Normal ⇄ Peaceful` — switchable in the pause menu (Peaceful = no hostile spawns).
- **Hardcore**: a permanent per-world flag set at creation (forces Survival + Normal; death deletes the world).

This follows Minecraft's real structure and still delivers the user's earlier Creative / Hardcore / Peaceful picks — now on their correct axes. **Zero new assets.** Save schema bumps **v7 → v8 (additive)**; no worldgen change. Single-player, so no "cheats" gate — mode/difficulty switch freely, except a **Hardcore world locks both**.

**Scope note:** this is large and cross-cutting → branch `feat/game-modes`, landed in focused, individually-green commit slices (data model → predicates → Creative → Spectator → Adventure → Hardcore → Peaceful → in-game switching → UI/HUD → docs/tests). Adventure is the cheapest and lowest-value (its purpose — locking block edits on shared custom maps — doesn't apply to a single-player game); it can be dropped to trim scope without affecting the rest.

## Mode behavior matrix

| Behavior | Survival | Creative | Adventure | Spectator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Damage / hunger / death | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Break blocks | ✓ | instant, no drop/durability | ✕ | ✕ |
| Place blocks | ✓ (consumes) | ✓ (no consume) | ✕ | ✕ |
| Flight | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ noclip |
| Terrain collision | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Interact (door/chest/trade/attack/eat/fish) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Mobs threaten player | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Inventory | normal | all-items palette | normal | hidden |
| Player render | solid | solid | solid | translucent |

## Mode predicates (the core abstraction)

New `lib/game/gameModes.ts` — `GameMode = "survival" | "creative" | "adventure" | "spectator"`, `Difficulty = "normal" | "peaceful"`, validators, and `GAME_MODE_PRESETS` / `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` (`{ id, label, blurb }`, parallel to `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS`). Plus intent predicates each system gates on (so no scattered string compares):

- `takesDamage(mode)` = survival | adventure
- `canEditBlocks(mode)` = survival | creative (adventure & spectator: false)
- `freeBuild(mode)` = creative (instant break, no drop, no consume)
- `canInteract(mode)` = mode !== spectator
- `canFly(mode)` = creative | spectator
- `isNoclip(mode)` = spectator
- `usesInventory(mode)` = mode !== spectator
- `mobsThreaten(mode)` = survival | adventure

## Data model & plumbing (copy the `worldType` pattern)

`worldType` is the proven per-world-enum template (validator → `WorldMeta` → `SaveData` additive + migration → `GameEngine` boot → `CreateWorldForm`). Mirror it:

1. **`WorldMeta`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore` (creation-time values for first boot + world-card badges); extend `sanitizeWorld` (coerce unknown → `survival`/`normal`/`false`) and `createWorld` deps.
2. **`SaveData` v8** (`lib/game/types.ts`): `version: 8; gameMode?; difficulty?; hardcore?` — authoritative *current* values (mode/difficulty may have been switched).
3. **Migration** (`lib/game/save.ts`): `migrateSaveV7toV8` pure bump; extend the `readSave` chain; repoint `SaveData` to v8.
4. **`GameEngine`** (`GameEngine.ts`): add the three to `GameEngineOptions`; resolve `save ?? options ?? default` (save wins on restore); `serialize()` writes them.
5. **`GameState`** (`engine/state.ts`): add `gameMode`, `difficulty`, `hardcore`, transient `isFlying`; expose all on the React snapshot for HUD/menus.

## Creative — gate via predicates

- **No damage / hunger / death** — `playerStats.ts` (`tickHungerDrain` skip; `tickHealthRegen` force full; gate `applyDamage` in water/lava/oxygen ticks), `playerMotion.ts` (fall + void damage), `playerLife.ts` (`applyDamageWithArmor`/`applyUnmitigatedDamage` early-return) — all gated on `!takesDamage(mode)`.
- **Free build** — `mining.ts` `tickMining`: when `freeBuild`, break instantly, skip `addBlockDrop` + `consumeToolDurability`; `placeSelectedBlock`: skip the `adjustSlotCount(-1)` decrement.
- **Flight** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isFlying`, replace gravity with vertical control (Space ascend / crouch descend / hover) at `FLY_SPEED`. `inputController.ts`: double-tap Space → `toggleFlight` when `canFly`.
- **All-items palette** — new tab in `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` listing `ITEM_DEFS` grouped by `kind` (reuse `inv-grid` buttons + `createSlot`/`adjustSlotCount`), with a search box; shown when `gameMode === "creative"`.

## Spectator — noclip free-cam

- **Always flying, noclip** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isNoclip`, skip the terrain collision-resolution/depenetration step and integrate position straight from velocity; force `isFlying` true, never grounded; reuse the Creative fly controls.
- **Invulnerable / no hunger / no death** — same `!takesDamage` gates as Creative.
- **No interaction at all** — gate all world-affecting commands in `GameEngine.dispatch` and `tickMining` behind `canInteract`: mining, placing, attack, use/eat/fish/trade/interact all no-op; only movement, camera, pause, and the mode menu remain.
- **Mobs ignore the player** — `mobAI.ts`/`projectileAI.ts`/`spawnDirector.ts` gate aggro + player-damage on `mobsThreaten(mode)` (false for Creative & Spectator).
- **Translucent player** — renderer: when spectator, draw the player model semi-transparent (or hidden in third-person); first-person is unchanged. Hide the hotbar/HUD bars.

## Adventure — survival minus terrain editing

- Identical to Survival (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trade/eat/fish all work) **except block break + place are disabled**: the `canEditBlocks` gate already added to `tickMining` (break) and `placeSelectedBlock` covers it. No flight, normal HUD. Essentially free once the predicate gates exist.

## Hardcore — permanent permadeath flag

- Fixed at creation; forces `gameMode = "survival"`, `difficulty = "normal"`, not switchable.
- On death in a hardcore world: don't respawn — leave `isDead` set and surface it; the React shell (`useMinecraftGame.ts` / `GameShell.tsx`) detects `isDead && hardcore`, shows a "Game Over" screen, calls the existing `deleteWorld(...)` (`lib/game/worlds.ts`), and returns to the world-select menu. Gate `tickRespawnTimer` so a hardcore player never auto-revives. World-card "Hardcore" badge; optional heart tint.

## Peaceful — a difficulty (no hostiles)

- Gate hostile spawning in `spawnDirector.ts` (`tickHostileSpawnDirector` + dungeon `tickSpawnerDirector`): early-return when `difficulty === "peaceful"` **or** `!mobsThreaten(mode)`. Clear existing hostiles on entering Peaceful. (monecraft hunger doesn't deal starvation damage, so no extra hunger handling needed.)

## In-game switching + state reset

- Pause menu gains a **Game Mode** selector (4 options) and **Difficulty** selector (2) — both hidden/locked for hardcore worlds.
- New `setGameMode` / `setDifficulty` engine commands. On switch, reset transient state so nothing leaks:
  - Entering a no-damage mode (Creative/Spectator): hearts/hunger forced full; reset lava/void/water/drown timers in `state.timers`.
  - Entering Spectator: `isFlying = true`, noclip on. Leaving Spectator: snap out of noclip (resolve out of any solid block, reuse the existing auto-unstuck depenetration), `isFlying = false`.
  - Entering Survival/Adventure: `isFlying = false` (gravity resumes); restore full hearts/hunger.
  - Entering Peaceful: clear hostiles.

## UI surfaces

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: a 4-option game-mode grid + 2-option difficulty grid + a Hardcore toggle (mirroring the `world-type-grid` markup). Thread through `WorldSelect.onCreate` → `createWorld({ gameMode, difficulty, hardcore })`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: world-card badges for mode/difficulty/hardcore.
- HUD (`components/game/*`): hide hearts + hunger in Creative/Spectator; hide the hotbar in Spectator; small "Creative"/"Spectator"/flying indicator; "Game Over" screen for hardcore death.
- Pause menu: the two selectors (locked for hardcore).

## Config tunables (`lib/game/config.ts`)

`FLY_SPEED` (≈12–16) and `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (0.3), under a new "Game modes / flight" group.

## Representative files

New: `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, `components/game/CreativeInventoryTab.tsx` (or inline).
Edited: `lib/game/types.ts`, `save.ts`, `worlds.ts`, `engine/state.ts`, `engine/GameEngine.ts`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`, `config.ts`, `input/inputController.ts`; systems `playerMotion.ts` / `playerStats.ts` / `playerLife.ts` / `mining.ts` / `spawnDirector.ts` / `mobAI.ts` / `projectileAI.ts`; the player renderer; components `CreateWorldForm.tsx` / `WorldSelect.tsx` / `InventoryPanel.tsx` / pause menu / HUD.

## Tests (colocated `*.test.ts`)

- Migration `v7 → v8` (old save → survival/normal/non-hardcore).
- Predicates table (each mode's flags).
- Creative: no damage, instant break, no drop/durability, no consume on place; palette inserts.
- Spectator: noclip (moves through a solid block), invulnerable, all interaction commands no-op, mobs don't aggro.
- Adventure: damage still applies; break + place are blocked; combat/interaction still work.
- Flight: `toggleFlight` only when `canFly`; ascend/descend change `velocity.y`.
- Hardcore: death sets `isDead`, no respawn, shell signal surfaced.
- Peaceful: hostile spawn directors no-op; hostiles cleared on switch.
- Switch resets timers + hearts/hunger + noclip exit. Update `config.test.ts` integrity (exhaustive presets, `ITEM_DEFS` palette coverage).

## Docs (ship with the change — part of the gate)

`docs/manual.md` (new "Game Modes" section: the four modes, flight, palette, Hardcore, Peaceful, switching), `docs/reference.md` (modes/difficulty table), `docs/save-format.md` (v8 fields + migration), `docs/tuning.md` (`FLY_SPEED` + double-tap), `README.md` (fly controls), `CHANGELOG.md` (`[Unreleased]`).

## Verification

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green; `bun run test:e2e` (touches input + shell).
- Manual pass (input/visual change): **Creative** — fly (double-tap Space), build from palette with no item loss, take no damage, hearts/hunger hidden. **Spectator** — fly through terrain, can't break/interact, mobs ignore you, player translucent. **Adventure** — take damage and fight mobs, but can't break/place blocks. **Hardcore** — die → world deleted → back to menu. **Peaceful** — no hostiles at night. **Switching** — flip modes/difficulty in the pause menu and confirm clean state resets; confirm hardcore worlds lock the selectors.

## After this lands

Other candidates remain for later: companions & taming, advancements & goals, building & decoration, water & exploration.

- **No damage / hunger / death** — `playerStats.ts` (`tickHungerDrain` skip; `tickHealthRegen` force full; gate `applyDamage` in water/lava/oxygen ticks), `playerMotion.ts` (fall + void damage), `playerLife.ts` (`applyDamageWithArmor`/`applyUnmitigatedDamage` early-return) — all gated on `!takesDamage(mode)`.
- **Free build** — `mining.ts` `tickMining`: when `freeBuild`, break instantly, skip `addBlockDrop` + `consumeToolDurability`; `placeSelectedBlock`: skip the `adjustSlotCount(-1)` decrement.

## Spectator — noclip free-cam

- **Always flying, noclip** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isNoclip`, skip the terrain collision-resolution/depenetration step and integrate position straight from velocity; force `isFlying` true, never grounded; reuse the Creative fly controls.
- **Invulnerable / no hunger / no death** — same `!takesDamage` gates as Creative.

## Adventure — survival minus terrain editing

Identical to Survival (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trade/eat/fish all work) **except block break + place are disabled** — covered by the `canEditBlocks` gate already added to `tickMining` (break) and `placeSelectedBlock`. No flight, normal HUD. Essentially free once the predicate gates exist.

## In-game switching + state reset

- Pause menu gains a **Game Mode** selector (4 options) using `GAME_MODE_PRESETS`.
- New `setGameMode` engine command. On switch, reset transient state so nothing leaks:
  - Entering a no-damage mode (Creative/Spectator): hearts/hunger forced full; reset lava/void/water/drown timers in `state.timers`.
  - Entering Spectator: `isFlying = true`, noclip on. Leaving Spectator: snap out of any solid block (reuse the existing auto-unstuck depenetration), `isFlying = false`.
  - Entering Survival/Adventure: `isFlying = false` (gravity resumes); restore full hearts/hunger.

## UI surfaces

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: a 4-option game-mode grid mirroring the existing `world-type-grid` markup; thread through `WorldSelect.onCreate` → `createWorld({ gameMode })`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: a world-card mode badge (like the current `worldType` sub-label).
- HUD (`components/game/*`): hide hearts + hunger in Creative/Spectator; hide the hotbar in Spectator; small "Creative"/"Spectator"/flying indicator.
- Pause menu: the mode selector.

## Config tunables (`lib/game/config.ts`)

`FLY_SPEED` (≈12–16) and `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (0.3), under a new "Game modes / flight" group.

## Representative files

New: `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, `components/game/CreativeInventoryTab.tsx` (or inline).
Edited: `lib/game/types.ts`, `save.ts`, `worlds.ts`, `engine/state.ts`, `engine/GameEngine.ts`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`, `config.ts`, `input/inputController.ts`; systems `playerMotion.ts` / `playerStats.ts` / `playerLife.ts` / `mining.ts` / `spawnDirector.ts` / `mobAI.ts` / `projectileAI.ts`; the player renderer; components `CreateWorldForm.tsx` / `WorldSelect.tsx` / `InventoryPanel.tsx` / pause menu / HUD.

- Migration `v7 → v8` (old save loads as `survival`).
- Predicates table (each mode's flags).

## Verification

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green; `bun run test:e2e` (touches input + shell).
- Manual pass (input/visual change): **Creative** — fly (double-tap Space), build from palette with no item loss, take no damage, hearts/hunger hidden. **Spectator** — fly through terrain, can't break/interact, mobs ignore you, player translucent. **Adventure** — take damage and fight mobs, but can't break/place blocks. **Switching** — flip modes in the pause menu and confirm clean state resets (flight off, HUD restored, no queued damage).

# Game Modes — Minecraft's four modes

## Context

monecraft is survival-only. We're adding Minecraft's four game modes as a single, self-contained axis: **Survival · Creative · Adventure · Spectator**, switchable in the pause menu. **Zero new assets.** Save schema bumps **v7 → v8** with one additive field (`gameMode`); no worldgen change. Single-player, so mode switches freely (no "cheats" gate).

**Deferred to a follow-up (explicitly out of scope now):** the **Difficulty** axis (`Peaceful`) and the **Hardcore** world flag (permadeath). They're orthogonal axes in Minecraft and drop in cleanly later — keeping them out now avoids touching the death/respawn + menu-shell deletion path and keeps this a focused change.

**Scope:** sizable but contained → branch `feat/game-modes`, landed in focused, individually-green commit slices (data model → predicates → Creative → Spectator → Adventure → in-game switching → UI/HUD → docs/tests). Adventure is the cheapest, lowest-value mode (its purpose — locking block edits on shared custom maps — barely applies to a single-player game) but nearly free once the predicate gates exist.

## Mode behavior matrix

| Behavior | Survival | Creative | Adventure | Spectator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Damage / hunger / death | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Break blocks | ✓ | instant, no drop/durability | ✕ | ✕ |
| Place blocks | ✓ (consumes) | ✓ (no consume) | ✕ | ✕ |
| Flight | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ noclip |
| Terrain collision | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Interact (door/chest/trade/attack/eat/fish) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Mobs threaten player | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Inventory | normal | all-items palette | normal | hidden |
| Player render | solid | solid | solid | translucent |

## Mode predicates (the core abstraction)

New `lib/game/gameModes.ts` — `GameMode = "survival" | "creative" | "adventure" | "spectator"`, an `isGameMode` validator, and `GAME_MODE_PRESETS` (`{ id, label, blurb }`, parallel to `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Plus intent predicates each system gates on (so no scattered string compares):

- `takesDamage(mode)` = survival | adventure
- `canEditBlocks(mode)` = survival | creative (adventure & spectator: false)
- `freeBuild(mode)` = creative (instant break, no drop, no consume)
- `canInteract(mode)` = mode !== spectator
- `canFly(mode)` = creative | spectator
- `isNoclip(mode)` = spectator
- `usesInventory(mode)` = mode !== spectator
- `mobsThreaten(mode)` = survival | adventure

## Data model & plumbing (copy the `worldType` pattern)

`worldType` is the proven per-world-enum template (validator → `WorldMeta` → `SaveData` additive + migration → `GameEngine` boot → `CreateWorldForm`). Mirror it for `gameMode`:

1. **`WorldMeta`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`): add `gameMode` (creation-time value for first boot + world-card badge); extend `sanitizeWorld` (unknown → `survival`) and `createWorld` deps.
2. **`SaveData` v8** (`lib/game/types.ts`): `SaveDataV8 = Omit<SaveDataV7,"version"> & { version: 8; gameMode?: GameMode }` — the authoritative *current* value (may have been switched in-game).
3. **Migration** (`lib/game/save.ts`): `migrateSaveV7toV8` pure bump; extend the `readSave` chain; repoint `SaveData` to v8.
4. **`GameEngine`** (`GameEngine.ts`): add `gameMode` to `GameEngineOptions`; resolve `save ?? options ?? "survival"` (save wins on restore, like `worldType`); `serialize()` writes it.
5. **`GameState`** (`engine/state.ts`): add `gameMode` and transient `isFlying`; expose both on the React snapshot for HUD/menus.

## Creative — gate via predicates

- **No damage / hunger / death** — `playerStats.ts` (`tickHungerDrain` skip; `tickHealthRegen` force full; gate `applyDamage` in water/lava/oxygen ticks), `playerMotion.ts` (fall + void damage), `playerLife.ts` (`applyDamageWithArmor`/`applyUnmitigatedDamage` early-return) — all gated on `!takesDamage(mode)`.
- **Free build** — `mining.ts` `tickMining`: when `freeBuild`, break instantly, skip `addBlockDrop` + `consumeToolDurability`; `placeSelectedBlock`: skip the `adjustSlotCount(-1)` decrement.
- **Flight** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isFlying`, replace gravity with vertical control (Space ascend / crouch descend / hover) at `FLY_SPEED`. `inputController.ts`: double-tap Space → `toggleFlight` when `canFly`.
- **All-items palette** — new tab in `components/game/InventoryPanel.tsx` listing `ITEM_DEFS` grouped by `kind` (reuse `inv-grid` buttons + `createSlot`/`adjustSlotCount`), with a search box; shown when `gameMode === "creative"`.

## Spectator — noclip free-cam

- **Always flying, noclip** — `playerMotion.ts`: when `isNoclip`, skip the terrain collision-resolution/depenetration step and integrate position straight from velocity; force `isFlying` true, never grounded; reuse the Creative fly controls.
- **Invulnerable / no hunger / no death** — same `!takesDamage` gates as Creative.
- **No interaction at all** — gate world-affecting commands in `GameEngine.dispatch` and `tickMining` behind `canInteract`: mining, placing, attack, use/eat/fish/trade/interact all no-op; only movement, camera, pause, and the mode menu remain.
- **Mobs ignore the player** — `mobAI.ts`/`projectileAI.ts`/`spawnDirector.ts` gate aggro + player-damage on `mobsThreaten(mode)` (false for Creative & Spectator).
- **Translucent player** — renderer: when spectator, draw the player model semi-transparent (or hidden in third-person); first-person unchanged. Hide the hotbar/HUD bars.

## Adventure — survival minus terrain editing

Identical to Survival (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trade/eat/fish all work) **except block break + place are disabled** — covered by the `canEditBlocks` gate already added to `tickMining` (break) and `placeSelectedBlock`. No flight, normal HUD. Essentially free once the predicate gates exist.

## In-game switching + state reset

- Pause menu gains a **Game Mode** selector (4 options) using `GAME_MODE_PRESETS`.
- New `setGameMode` engine command. On switch, reset transient state so nothing leaks:
  - Entering a no-damage mode (Creative/Spectator): hearts/hunger forced full; reset lava/void/water/drown timers in `state.timers`.
  - Entering Spectator: `isFlying = true`, noclip on. Leaving Spectator: snap out of any solid block (reuse the existing auto-unstuck depenetration), `isFlying = false`.
  - Entering Survival/Adventure: `isFlying = false` (gravity resumes); restore full hearts/hunger.

## UI surfaces

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: a 4-option game-mode grid mirroring the existing `world-type-grid` markup; thread through `WorldSelect.onCreate` → `createWorld({ gameMode })`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: a world-card mode badge (like the current `worldType` sub-label).
- HUD (`components/game/*`): hide hearts + hunger in Creative/Spectator; hide the hotbar in Spectator; small "Creative"/"Spectator"/flying indicator.
- Pause menu: the mode selector.

## Config tunables (`lib/game/config.ts`)

`FLY_SPEED` (≈12–16) and `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (0.3), under a new "Game modes / flight" group.

## Representative files

New: `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, `components/game/CreativeInventoryTab.tsx` (or inline).
Edited: `lib/game/types.ts`, `save.ts`, `worlds.ts`, `engine/state.ts`, `engine/GameEngine.ts`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`, `config.ts`, `input/inputController.ts`; systems `playerMotion.ts` / `playerStats.ts` / `playerLife.ts` / `mining.ts` / `spawnDirector.ts` / `mobAI.ts` / `projectileAI.ts`; the player renderer; components `CreateWorldForm.tsx` / `WorldSelect.tsx` / `InventoryPanel.tsx` / pause menu / HUD.

## Tests (colocated `*.test.ts`)

- Migration `v7 → v8` (old save loads as `survival`).
- Predicates table (each mode's flags).
- Creative: no damage, instant break, no drop/durability, no consume on place; palette inserts.
- Spectator: noclip (moves through a solid block), invulnerable, all interaction commands no-op, mobs don't aggro.
- Adventure: damage still applies; break + place blocked; combat/interaction still work.
- Flight: `toggleFlight` only when `canFly`; ascend/descend change `velocity.y`.
- Switch resets timers + hearts/hunger + noclip exit. Update `config.test.ts` integrity (exhaustive presets, `ITEM_DEFS` palette coverage).

## Docs (ship with the change — part of the gate)

`docs/manual.md` (new "Game Modes" section: the four modes, flight, palette, switching), `docs/reference.md` (modes table), `docs/save-format.md` (v8 field + migration), `docs/tuning.md` (`FLY_SPEED` + double-tap), `README.md` (fly controls), `CHANGELOG.md` (`[Unreleased]`).

## Verification

- Gate: `bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green; `bun run test:e2e` (touches input + shell).
- Manual pass (input/visual change): **Creative** — fly (double-tap Space), build from palette with no item loss, take no damage, hearts/hunger hidden. **Spectator** — fly through terrain, can't break/interact, mobs ignore you, player translucent. **Adventure** — take damage and fight mobs, but can't break/place blocks. **Switching** — flip modes in the pause menu and confirm clean state resets (flight off, HUD restored, no queued damage).

## Next time (deferred)

- **Difficulty axis** (`Normal ⇄ Peaceful`) — switchable; Peaceful gates hostile spawns. The `mobsThreaten`/spawn gates added here are the hook it plugs into.
- **Hardcore** world flag — one life; death deletes the world (touches respawn + the menu-shell `deleteWorld` flow).

=== CHANGELOG top ===
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21

### Added

- **XP & enchanting**: the game gains its first progression currency and a way to spend it, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural XP bar + effect-coloured table sprite, synthesized blip/shimmer). The save schema bumps **v6 → v7** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **XP** (`state.xp`, banked points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level): earned from **mob kills** (hostiles more than passives, the **boss a jackpot**; babies give none, like drops — table in `mobXp.ts`), **mining ores** (scaled by rarity), and **fishing** catches. A green **XP bar** above the hotbar fills toward the next level with the level number over it. Unlike status effects, XP is a long-term currency and is **not cleared on death**
=== save-format headings ===
1:# Save format & compatibility
3:## Schema
5:`SaveData` (version 7) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
21:Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
23:Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
33:### Version history
35:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
36:- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.

51:## Profiles & worlds
53:Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):

=== README 21-34 ===
## Controls

- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, or throw a selected spear
- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
- `Esc`: Pause menu (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, sound/music volume sliders, and the Appearance skin picker live there) · `F3`: Debug overlay

New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.

=== manual 54-76 ===
## Controls

| Key / input        | Action                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                |
| `Space`            | Jump                                                                |
| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                   |
| `W` + `CapsLock`   | Sprint — faster, but drains hunger                                  |
| Mouse              | Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)       |
| Left-click (hold)  | Break the targeted block / attack a mob                             |
| Right-click or `E` | Place/interact, or throw a selected spear                           |
| `1`–`9`            | Select a hotbar slot                                                |
| `I`                | Open / close inventory & crafting                                   |
| `F`                | Eat the selected food, or drink a selected potion                   |
| `V`                | Cycle camera: first-person → third-person rear → third-person front |
| `Shift` + `U`      | Emergency unstuck (teleport to safe ground if wedged)               |
| `Esc`              | Pause menu (save / load / reset, volume sliders, skin picker)       |
| `F3`               | Debug overlay (FPS, position, daylight, mob counts)                 |

Gameplay is always **eye-relative**: even in third person, your reach, aim, and
audio follow where your eyes point, and the crosshair stays centered.

## Survival
=== reference 11-24 ===
## World types

Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.

| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |

## Recipes
=== tuning 15-27 ===
## Player feel — physics & movement

`GRAVITY`, `JUMP_VELOCITY`, `WALK_SPEED`, `SPRINT_SPEED`, `CROUCH_SPEED`,
`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.

Read by `systems/playerMotion.ts`. These set the moment-to-moment feel.
`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.

Single-player and client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved to localStorage.

bun install
bun run dev

Gameplay is always **eye-relative**: even in third person, your reach, aim, and
audio follow where your eyes point, and the crosshair stays centered.

## Game modes

Pick a mode when you create a world (next to the name, world type, and seed), and
switch it any time from the **pause menu** (`Esc` → Game Mode). It's saved with the
world. Modes are independent of the world type.

- **Survival** — the standard game: gather, craft, fight, and manage health and
  hunger. You can die.
- **Creative** — build freely. You fly (double-tap `Space`, then `Space` / `C` to
  rise and descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly,
  and place blocks without using them up. The recipe book is replaced by a
  searchable **palette of every item** — click one to drop a stack into your
  inventory.
- **Adventure** — survival in every way (damage, hunger, mobs, combat,
  doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built
  world stays as-is.
- **Spectator** — a free camera: you fly through walls (noclip), are invisible and
  invulnerable, and can't interact with anything. Mobs ignore you entirely. There's
  no hotbar or status bars — just look around.

Switching modes refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, so it's
always safe to flip between them.

# Save format & compatibility

## Schema

`SaveData` (version 7) in `lib/game/types.ts`:

- world `seed`
- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
- inventory slots with durability **and enchantments** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`). The same path serializes chest contents
- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
- equipped armor
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
- `effects` (optional) — active status effects as `{ id, remaining }[]` (remaining in seconds). Drink-granted buffs (Speed/Strength/Regeneration/Fire Resistance/Water Breathing) and the rotten-flesh Poison hazard live in `state.effects` (a Map) and persist here, but are **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active at save time. On load, `restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops unknown ids and non-positive/garbage durations
- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`

Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)

Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.

**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.

Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
(breath restores to full). The status-effect **accumulators** (`effectRegenTimer`,
`effectPoisonTimer`) are likewise transient — but the effects **themselves**
(`state.effects`) persist via the `effects` field above and survive a reload.

### Version history

- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Game modes**: the game gains Minecraft's four ways to play — **Survival** (the original), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator** — as a single per-player axis you pick at world creation and can switch any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide
  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact

51:8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
52:9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
53:10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
54:11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
55:12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
56:13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)
58:**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.
62:Combat (`systems/combat.ts`) runs on the `attack` command rather than per frame: a held bow branches to `tryFireBow` (instant click-to-fire, no draw-charge), a spear melees at its longer `weaponReach`, and otherwise `tryAttackMob` swings. The `placeBlock` command runs a fixed right-click precedence (`systems/interact.ts` + engine): throw the selected spear (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`) → feed an aimed animal (`tryFeedAimedMob`) → interact with the aimed block (`tryInteractBlock`, e.g. bed/furnace/chest/door) → summon the boss from a Cursed Totem (`trySummonBoss`) → use the held item (`tryUseHeldItem`, e.g. hoe tills soil, seeds plant a crop) → `placeSelectedBlock` — so each interaction consumes the click instead of getting a block placed against it. New mechanics get a new system module and a slot in this sequence — don't grow the engine class with inline logic.
66:**Dungeon loot chests.** Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents can't ride the block-diff baseline. The engine instead keeps two session-only sets — `dungeonChestIndices` / `dungeonSpawnerIndices` — rebuilt each boot from the seed via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`, which replays the dungeon placement math without writing blocks), plus a **persisted** `lootedDungeonChests` set. On a dungeon chest's first open or break, `systems/dungeon.ts` `fillDungeonChestIfUnlooted` rolls loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`) and marks the index looted. Gating on the looted set — not on whether the chest is currently non-empty — is what stops an emptied-then-reloaded chest from re-rolling (an empty container is dropped from `blockEntities`).

84:## Audio (`lib/game/audio/`)
95:## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)
99:**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). ## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)

- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command)`, advances `step(dt, input)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`) and the world size is overridable for fast headless tests.
- `state.ts` — `GameState` (player with `yaw`/`pitch`, inventory, mobs and thrown
  spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, mining
  progress, timers) plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
- `blockChanges.ts` — the delta tracker behind the save format: tracked block writes against the worldgen baseline; reverted edits drop out of the save.
- `systems/` — one module per mechanic, each a function over `GameState`:

### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)

0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
1. Stuck detection / auto-unstuck (`STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`)
2. Death check + respawn countdown (while dead, only mobs tick)
3. Sleep gate: while `state.sleepTimer > 0`, `step` decrements the fade and returns (full freeze, like pause); at zero it skips the clock to the next morning
4. Player movement & physics (`systems/playerMotion.ts` — derives direction from `yaw`, scratch vectors, no per-frame allocations)
5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
6. Mining progress and block breaking (`systems/mining.ts`; placement also lives here)
7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula); immediately after, `systems/weather.ts` sets the **transient** `state.weather` (rain/snow/clear) as a pure function of `dayClock` + seed — cosmetic only: never serialized, never touches spawn/daylight balance
8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)

**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.

**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new `"boss"` kind requires entries in all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `MOB_DROPS`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).

+**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.

Combat (`systems/combat.ts`) runs on the `attack` command rather than per frame: a held bow branches to `tryFireBow` (instant click-to-fire, no draw-charge), a spear melees at its longer `weaponReach`, and otherwise `tryAttackMob` swings. The `placeBlock` command runs a fixed right-click precedence (`systems/interact.ts` + engine): throw the selected spear (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`) → feed an aimed animal (`tryFeedAimedMob`) → interact with the aimed block (`tryInteractBlock`, e.g. bed/furnace/chest/door) → summon the boss from a Cursed Totem (`trySummonBoss`) → use the held item (`tryUseHeldItem`, e.g. hoe tills soil, seeds plant a crop) → `placeSelectedBlock` — so each interaction consumes the click instead of getting a block placed against it. New mechanics get a new system module and a slot in this sequence — don't grow the engine class with inline logic.

**Block-entities (chest contents).** Blocks are bare `BlockId`s, but a chest needs attached storage, so `state.containers: Map<voxelIndex, InventorySlot[]>` holds each placed chest's slots (keyed by `world.index`, the same space as the block diff). Placing a chest creates an empty entry; opening one (`interactChest`) sets `state.openContainerIndex` and `inventoryOpen` so the panel renders its grid; the `moveStack` command shuttles slots across the inventory/chest boundary (chest indices offset by `CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE`); breaking a chest spills its contents into the inventory via `inventory.tryInsertSlots` (refused if they don't fit). `serialize()` persists non-empty containers as `blockEntities`; see [save-format.md](save-format.md).

1	# Player Manual
2	
3	A complete guide to playing Monecraft — a single-player, browser-based voxel
4	sandbox. Mine, build, craft, farm, fight off the night, and survive.
5	
6	This page is the prose guide; for the exact numbers (every recipe, block, mob, and
7	item stat) see the [reference tables](reference.md). Just want the keys? They're in
8	the [README](../README.md#controls).
9	
10	> Everything you see and hear is generated from code at runtime — there are no
11	> image or audio files anywhere in the game.
12	
13	## Worlds & profiles
14	
15	The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:
16	
17	1. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
18	   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
19	   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
20	2. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
21	   you name it, choose a **world type** (Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands —
22	   see [the reference](reference.md#world-types)), and optionally enter a **seed** —
23	   type a number or a word to get the same world every time, or leave it blank for a
24	   random one. Worlds you've played show most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
25	3. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
26	   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
27	   world you were in.
28	
29	Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
30	deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.
31	
32	## Getting started: your first day
33	
34	You spawn at dawn on solid ground with a small starter kit: stacks of grass, dirt,
35	stone, wood, planks, cobble, and sand, plus a **wood pickaxe** and a **knife**.
36	
37	The day-night cycle is short — **four minutes per full day** — so the first night
38	comes fast. A good opening:
39	
40	1. **Look around.** Double-click the game to lock the mouse (the starting gesture
41	   doesn't mine). Move with `W A S D`, look with the mouse.
42	2. **Gear up from your kit.** Open the inventory with **`I`**. You already have
43	   cobble and wood, so craft a **stone pickaxe** (2 cobble + 1 wood) and a **stone
44	   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
45	   knife.
46	3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for
47	   more materials; craft **2 wood → 4 planks** whenever you need them.
48	4. **Shelter before dark.** Wall yourself in with blocks (**right-click** or `E`
49	   to place the selected hotbar item), or craft a **bed** and skip the night
50	   entirely. Hostile mobs spawn once it gets dark, so don't be caught in the open.
51	
52	From there it's a sandbox: dig for ores, build, farm, breed animals, and gear up.
53	
54	## Controls
55	
56	| Key / input        | Action                                                                                |
57	| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
58	| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                                  |
59	| `Space`            | Jump                                                                                  |
60	| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                                     |
61	| `W` + `CapsLock`   | Sprint — faster, but drains hunger                                                    |
62	| Double-tap `Space` | Toggle flight (Creative / Spectator); then `Space` / `C` rise/descend                 |
63	| Mouse              | Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)                         |
64	| Left-click (hold)  | Break the targeted block / attack a mob                                               |
65	| Right-click or `E` | Place/interact, or throw a selected spear                                             |
66	| `1`–`9`            | Select a hotbar slot                                                                  |
67	| `I`                | Open / close inventory & crafting                                                     |
68	| `F`                | Eat the selected food, or drink a selected potion                                     |
69	| `V`                | Cycle camera: first-person → third-person rear → third-person front                   |
70	| `Shift` + `U`      | Emergency unstuck (teleport to safe ground if wedged)                                 |
71	| `Esc`              | Pause menu (save / load / reset, **Game Mode** switcher, volume sliders, skin picker) |
72	| `F3`               | Debug overlay (FPS, position, daylight, mob counts)                                   |
73	
74	Gameplay is always **eye-relative**: even in third person, your reach, aim, and
75	audio follow where your eyes point, and the crosshair stays centered.
76	
77	## Game modes
78	
79	Pick a mode when you create a world (next to the name, world type, and seed), and
80	switch it any time from the **pause menu** (`Esc` → Game Mode). It's saved with the
81	world. Modes are independent of the world type.
82	
83	- **Survival** — the standard game: gather, craft, fight, and manage health and
84	  hunger. You can die.
85	- **Creative** — build freely. You fly (double-tap `Space`, then `Space` / `C` to
86	  rise and descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly,
87	  and place blocks without using them up. The recipe book is replaced by a
88	  searchable **palette of every item** — click one to drop a stack into your
89	  inventory.
90	- **Adventure** — survival in every way (damage, hunger, mobs, combat,
91	  doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built
92	  world stays as-is.
93	- **Spectator** — a free camera: you fly through walls (noclip), are invisible and
94	  invulnerable, and can't interact with anything. Mobs ignore you entirely. There's
95	  no hotbar or status bars — just look around.
96	
97	Switching modes refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, so it's
98	always safe to flip between them.
99	
100	## Survival
101	
102	### Health and death
103	
104	You have **20 health**, shown as **10 hearts** (each heart = 2 HP). Mobs, falling
105	into the void, and starvation-adjacent danger chip it away. At zero health you die,
106	freeze for **3 seconds**, then respawn — at your bed if you've slept in one,
107	otherwise at a random land point. Death doesn't wipe your world or inventory.
108	
109	If you ever get wedged inside terrain, press **`Shift`+`U`** to teleport free. (Standing in
110	water is _not_ "stuck" — you're allowed to swim.) You can place blocks into water
111	to replace water cells when building underwater. Do not remain continuously
112	immersed for more than **60 seconds**: after that grace period you take **1.5
113	hearts every second**, ignoring armor. Leaving the water resets the timer.
114	
115	### Caves are dark — carry a torch
116	
117	Underground is now genuinely **dark**: sunlight reaches down open shafts and
118	spills a little way into cave mouths, but the deep tunnels are pitch black. Craft
119	**torches** (1 coal + 1 wood → 4 torches) and place them as you explore — each casts
120	a warm pool of light that won't fade at night. Without a light source you're mining
121	blind, and the dark is where monsters lurk. **Coal** is the shallow, common ore you
122	mine for torch and furnace fuel — if you're out, smelt a log into **charcoal**, which
123	works the same.
124	
125	### Drowning and lava
126	
127	When your **head** goes underwater a row of **air bubbles** appears above the
128	hunger bar and drains over about 15 seconds; once it's empty you start **drowning**
129	(1 heart/second until you surface). Bubbles refill almost instantly when your head
130	comes up. (This is separate from the slow 60-second immersion damage above — wading
131	chest-deep never drowns you.)
132	
133	**Lava** pools in the deepest caves and glows in the dark. It is a death trap:

25

Adds Minecraft's four game modes as a single per-player axis: **Survival** (the existing game), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator**. Pick a mode when you create a world (next to world type and seed) and switch it any time from the pause menu. Zero new assets; save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with no worldgen change.

## Modes

| Mode | Damage / hunger | Break / place | Flight | Interact | Mobs | Inventory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Survival | yes | yes | no | yes | hostile | normal |
| Creative | no | instant, free | yes | yes | ignore you | all-items palette |
| Adventure | yes | **no** | no | yes | hostile | normal |
| Spectator | no | no | yes (noclip) | **no** | ignore you | hidden |

- **Creative** — fly (double-tap `Space`, then `Space`/`C` to rise/descend), invulnerable, no hunger, instant break of any block, place without consuming. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item**.
- **Adventure** — survival in every way except you can't break or place blocks.
- **Spectator** — a free camera: fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, no interaction; hostiles ignore you and the HUD/hotbar hide.
- **Switching** mid-game refills bars, clears pending hazard damage, matches flight to the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator.

## Design

A new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than scattering `mode === "x"` checks. So the four modes share one set of seams: the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`, HUD in `MinecraftGame.tsx`.

`gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's the **current, switchable** value; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. New commands: `setGameMode`, `toggleFlight`, `creativeGiveItem`. New tunables: `FLY_SPEED`, `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`.

Built as 8 focused, individually-green commits (plumbing → creative → palette → spectator → adventure → switching/UI → docs → e2e fixes).

## Deferred (follow-up)

The **Difficulty** axis (Peaceful) and the **Hardcore** flag are intentionally out of scope here — they're orthogonal axes in Minecraft and plug into the same predicate/spawn seams later.

## Verification

- `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check` clean
- `bun test`: **708 pass / 0 fail** (+38 new tests covering the predicate table, the v7→v8 migration, and each mode's behavior)
- `bun run build` green
- `bun run test:e2e`: **16 pass**

Docs updated: manual, reference, save-format, tuning, architecture, testing, README, and a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.
EOF

58	- **Upstream contribution**: PR **davidhu0527/monecraft#7** (`hutusi:main`→`davidhu0527:main`, full 36-commit fork divergence — caves & lighting can't be cleanly isolated since it sits on the dungeon/endgame stack) is now **MERGED** (see the v0.9.0 status block at the top for the current, post-#7 upstream gap).

Per-voxel light engine (`lib/world/lighting.ts`: packed sky+block 0–15, derived cache never serialized, full bake at load + Minecraft-style remove/refill `applyEdit` on every edit via the `blockChanges.set` chokepoint), mesher `aLight` attribute, and a `GameRenderer` `onBeforeCompile` shader patch that gates terrain by sky-exposure (caves dark) + adds block-light glow — **day/night via the existing scene lights, no uniform, no re-mesh** (refined the planned uDayFactor away). Torches (craft 4 from 1 wood, emit 14), deep-cave **lava** (worldgen-only, emit 15, burns on contact), **drowning** bubble meter (head-cell, coexists with the 60s body-immersion timer). **`SAVE_KEY` bumped v6→v7** (lava worldgen re-baseline; payload schema unchanged at v5 — nothing new persisted). All gates green (lint/typecheck/format/458 tests/build/e2e 10/10); **a human visual pass on the dark caves + torch/lava glow + drowning bubbles is still recommended** (per docs/testing.md, couldn't do it headless).
63	
64	The roadmap is now essentially exhausted — every major direction (UI, juice, chests, dungeons, endgame/ranged, upstream sync, caves & lighting) has shipped or is built. Likely next acts are non-feature: cut the long-pending release (package.json bump + roll `[Unreleased]` → a version + tag) once caves & lighting merges, or polish. The game has caves (now dark), ores, ~120 houses, 5 biomes, water+lava, 6 mobs + a boss, farming/breeding/cooking/beds, 7-tier gear + bow + spears, chests, dungeons, doors, torches, and per-voxel lighting. See [[review-fixes-no-push]] and [[no-pr-attribution]] for workflow preferences.
65

# Monecraft (Next.js + TypeScript + Three.js + Bun)

[![CI](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/hutusi/monecraft?label=release&sort=semver)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/tags)

A playable, Minecraft-inspired voxel game that runs entirely in your browser. Explore procedural terrain across five biomes and dig into **dark caves** — lit only by the torches you craft and place, where lava pools and mobs lurk. Mine ores, raid **underground dungeons** for loot, build and farm, breed animals, craft through seven gear tiers up to a **bow** and throwable **spears**, and take on an **endgame boss** for a true win condition — all across a day-night cycle with hunger, drowning, and lava hazards.

The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player and client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved to localStorage.

## Run

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000`.

The game opens to a menu: pick or create a **profile** (your name and look), then create or choose a **world** to play. New worlds let you pick a **type** — Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands — and a seed. Each profile keeps its own list of worlds, so several players can share one browser. Inside the game, **Esc → Save & Quit to Worlds** returns to the world list.

## Controls

- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
- Double-tap `Space`: Toggle flight (Creative / Spectator); then `Space` / `C` to rise / descend
- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, or throw a selected spear
- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
- `Esc`: Pause menu (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, the **Game Mode** switcher, sound/music volume sliders, and the Appearance skin picker live there) · `F3`: Debug overlay

New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.

## Development

```bash
bun run lint        # ESLint
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
bun test            # unit + integration + component tests
bun run build       # production build
bun run test:e2e    # Playwright browser smoke tests
bun run format      # Prettier
```

All of these are enforced by CI on every PR. The game simulation is a headless engine (no DOM), so gameplay logic is covered by real simulation tests, and a Playwright smoke suite exercises the browser layers — see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).

## Docs

- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide: getting started, survival, crafting, mobs, farming
- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — scannable tables: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item stats
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/shell layering and invariants
- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — add a block, item, recipe, mob, or mechanic
- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema and compatibility rules
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — workflow and verification baseline

1	# Player Manual
2	
3	A complete guide to playing Monecraft — a single-player, browser-based voxel
4	sandbox. Mine, build, craft, farm, fight off the night, and survive.
5	
6	This page is the prose guide; for the exact numbers (every recipe, block, mob, and
7	item stat) see the [reference tables](reference.md). Just want the keys? They're in
8	the [README](../README.md#controls).
9	
10	> Everything you see and hear is generated from code at runtime — there are no
11	> image or audio files anywhere in the game.
12	
13	## Worlds & profiles
14	
15	The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:
16	
17	1. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
18	   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
19	   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
20	2. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
21	   you name it, choose a **world type** (Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands —
22	   see [the reference](reference.md#world-types)), and optionally enter a **seed** —
23	   type a number or a word to get the same world every time, or leave it blank for a
24	   random one. Worlds you've played show most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
25	3. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
26	   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
27	   world you were in.
28	
29	Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
30	deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.
31	
32	## Getting started: your first day
33	
34	You spawn at dawn on solid ground with a small starter kit: stacks of grass, dirt,
35	stone, wood, planks, cobble, and sand, plus a **wood pickaxe** and a **knife**.
36	
37	The day-night cycle is short — **four minutes per full day** — so the first night
38	comes fast. A good opening:
39	
40	1. **Look around.** Double-click the game to lock the mouse (the starting gesture
41	   doesn't mine). Move with `W A S D`, look with the mouse.
42	2. **Gear up from your kit.** Open the inventory with **`I`**. You already have
43	   cobble and wood, so craft a **stone pickaxe** (2 cobble + 1 wood) and a **stone
44	   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
45	   knife.
46	3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for
47	   more materials; craft **2 wood → 4 planks** whenever you need them.
48	4. **Shelter before dark.** Wall yourself in with blocks (**right-click** or `E`
49	   to place the selected hotbar item), or craft a **bed** and skip the night
50	   entirely. Hostile mobs spawn once it gets dark, so don't be caught in the open.
51	
52	From there it's a sandbox: dig for ores, build, farm, breed animals, and gear up.
53	
54	## Controls
55	
56	| Key / input        | Action                                                                                      |
57	| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
58	| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                                        |
59	| `Space`            | Jump                                                                                        |
60	| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                                           |
61	| `W` + `CapsLock`   | Sprint — faster, but drains hunger                                                          |
62	| Double-tap `Space` | Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); `Space` / `C` rise/descend while flying |
63	| Mouse              | Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)                               |
64	| Left-click (hold)  | Break the targeted block / attack a mob                                                     |
65	| Right-click or `E` | Place/interact, or throw a selected spear                                                   |
66	| `1`–`9`            | Select a hotbar slot                                                                        |
67	| `I`                | Open / close inventory & crafting                                                           |
68	| `F`                | Eat the selected food, or drink a selected potion                                           |
69	| `V`                | Cycle camera: first-person → third-person rear → third-person front                         |
70	| `Shift` + `U`      | Emergency unstuck (teleport to safe ground if wedged)                                       |
71	| `Esc`              | Pause menu (save / load / reset, **Game Mode** switcher, volume sliders, skin picker)       |
72	| `F3`               | Debug overlay (FPS, position, daylight, mob counts)                                         |
73	
74	Gameplay is always **eye-relative**: even in third person, your reach, aim, and
75	audio follow where your eyes point, and the crosshair stays centered.
76	
77	## Game modes
78	
79	Pick a mode when you create a world (next to the name, world type, and seed), and
80	switch it any time from the **pause menu** (`Esc` → Game Mode). It's saved with the
81	world. Modes are independent of the world type.
82	
83	- **Survival** — the standard game: gather, craft, fight, and manage health and
84	  hunger. You can die.
85	- **Creative** — build freely. You fly (double-tap `Space`, then `Space` / `C` to
86	  rise and descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly,
87	  and place blocks without using them up. The recipe book is replaced by a
88	  searchable **palette of every item** — click one to drop a stack into your
89	  inventory.
90	- **Adventure** — survival in every way (damage, hunger, mobs, combat,
91	  doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built
92	  world stays as-is.
93	- **Spectator** — a free camera: you fly through walls (noclip), are invisible and
94	  invulnerable, and can't interact with anything. Mobs ignore you entirely. There's
95	  no hotbar or status bars — just look around.
96	
97	Switching modes refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, so it's
98	always safe to flip between them.
99	
100	## Survival
101	
102	### Health and death
103	
104	You have **20 health**, shown as **10 hearts** (each heart = 2 HP). Mobs, falling
105	into the void, and starvation-adjacent danger chip it away. At zero health you die,
106	freeze for **3 seconds**, then respawn — at your bed if you've slept in one,
107	otherwise at a random land point. Death doesn't wipe your world or inventory.
108	
109	If you ever get wedged inside terrain, press **`Shift`+`U`** to teleport free. (Standing in
110	water is _not_ "stuck" — you're allowed to swim.) You can place blocks into water
111	to replace water cells when building underwater. Do not remain continuously
112	immersed for more than **60 seconds**: after that grace period you take **1.5
113	hearts every second**, ignoring armor. Leaving the water resets the timer.
114	
115	### Caves are dark — carry a torch
116	
117	Underground is now genuinely **dark**: sunlight reaches down open shafts and
118	spills a little way into cave mouths, but the deep tunnels are pitch black. Craft
119	**torches** (1 coal + 1 wood → 4 torches) and place them as you explore — each casts
120	a warm pool of light that won't fade at night. Without a light source you're mining
121	blind, and the dark is where monsters lurk. **Coal** is the shallow, common ore you
122	mine for torch and furnace fuel — if you're out, smelt a log into **charcoal**, which
123	works the same.
124	
125	### Drowning and lava
126	
127	When your **head** goes underwater a row of **air bubbles** appears above the
128	hunger bar and drains over about 15 seconds; once it's empty you start **drowning**
